title: A0/U1 amendment: atomic split-measure plan variant for overfill resolution
description:
Deferred by the U1/spec leaf (jcpe-milestone-reliable-studio-l3a.10.1) and recorded in docs/U1_EDITING_CONTRACT.md section 5.3 plus tests/fixtures/editing/u1-editing-contract.json handoff.deferredToDependentLeaves.

## Problem
REBUILD_PLAN 17.4 requires a duration edit that overfills a measure to offer 'Split at bar', 'Move following events', or 'Cancel'. Only the last two are expressible with one accepted A0 command today:
- Move following events = one 'move' command (targets = the overflow events, destination = the next measure, completionUpdates covering both measures).
- Split at bar would require inserting a new empty measure AND moving existing events into it while preserving their stable identities. That is two commands, so it cannot be one atomic, singly-undoable user action.

U1 v1 therefore states the overfill with its exact current fill, resulting fill, and bar capacity, and offers Move following events / Shorten the duration / Cancel. It never silently rebalances or drops beats. This is honest but incomplete against the plan text.

## Required work
Amend the A0/U1 atomic edit-plan contract (docs/A0_U1_ATOMIC_EDIT_PLAN_CONTRACT.md, src/application/application-edit-plan-contract.ts) with a sixth plan variant, provisionally 'split-measure': one source measure, one interior before-event boundary, exact rational partition of the measure total, stable identities preserved for every moved event, one fresh measure id, exact completion declarations for both resulting measures, its own refusal codes, bookmark mapping rows, and work counters. Then wire U1 operation U1-OP-013's sibling 'split-at-bar' row.

## Constraints
Same discipline as the accepted R1 packet: independently authored literal transitions, exact counters, undo/redo trios, collision and plus-one boundaries, mutation controls, and reciprocal trace/provenance links. The existing five plan kinds and the historical fifteen command kinds must not change. Do not weaken the one-command-per-gesture rule to work around the gap.

## Exit criteria
The amendment ships with its validator oracle, static test, production conformance witnesses, and a U1 operation row whose channel binding the U1 validator accepts.

title: Owner arbitration: T0 custom-chord syntax gap narrows the M0 'Custom chord' mandate
description: The owner's MIDI-import mandate (jcpe-v3c2) says a sonority with no confident symbol should be offered as 'the literal pitch set as a Custom chord rather than inventing a name'. Two owner options: (a) accept this honest degradation as the standing behavior; (b) mandate a T0 grammar amendment adding a custom/literal-pitch-set chord syntax (heavy: grammar freeze, parser, formatter, voicing/playback story for unnamed sonorities). Related shipped limit, same bead: quick entry caps one draft at 4,096 code points, so an import exceeding that is refused with the count stated rather than chunked (chunking would break the one-undoable-edit law) — confirm this refusal is the wanted behavior for large files. Decide before or during jcpe-v3c2.3 verify design; the verify leaf proves shipped behavior either way.
close_reason: DECIDED (owner delegated 2026-08-05, CrimsonBeaver): option (a) — the honest degradation stands. A sonority the grammar cannot name is STATED with its literal pitch classes and evidence and writes no chord; nothing is invented. Rationale: the T0 grammar freeze is load-bearing across parser/formatter/voicing/playback, and a literal-pitch-set syntax has no voicing/playback story without a V0 amendment — exactly the work jcpe-qyyn's Advanced lane (writing custom sonorities as literal events) would carry if the owner later mandates it; that bead now owns option (b). title: Disable Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon injection for jazzchords.org (CSP correctly blocks it; edge modifies released bytes)
description: Reported by the owner 2026-07-28: Chrome console on jazzchords.org shows the embedded CSP blocking https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js. Diagnosis: Cloudflare Web Analytics auto-injection inserts its telemetry script into served HTML at the edge (a curl fetch of the same URL shows no beacon tag — injection is response/UA dependent). The block itself is CORRECT behavior: the artifact's hash-based CSP exists precisely to refuse unauthorized scripts, and the product boundary (AGENTS.md: no telemetry, no CDN, no runtime network dependency) forbids this beacon. Two real problems remain: (1) the boundary violation — an analytics script is being attached to a product that promises none; (2) integrity — the edge is modifying the served artifact, so served bytes no longer match the reviewed release and the console error will alarm users. title: A0/U1 split-measure/spec: Specify the sixth plan variant, laws, and independent fixtures
close_reason:
The sixth atomic plan variant is specified, machine-checkable, and additive. Nothing in the accepted R1 packet changed, and every gate stayed green throughout.

## The design

`split-measure` is `split-section` one level down.

```text
kind:                   "split-measure"
measureId:              MeasureId
beforeEventId:          ChordEventId        // first event of the suffix, strict interior
firstMeasureTotal:      BeatDuration        // exact sum of the retained events
secondMeasureTotal:     BeatDuration        // exact sum of the moved events
newMeasureCompletion:   MeasureCompletion   // the fresh measure's declaration
completionDeclarations: readonly [AtomicEditPlanCompletionDeclaration]
identityPolicy:         "retain-source-prefix-allocate-suffix"
eventPolicy:            "move-suffix-preserve-identities"
```

Three decisions worth recording:

**Two declarations, one row.** A caller cannot name an ID that does not exist yet, so the fresh measure's completion is a dedicated `newMeasureCompletion` field rather than a second `completionDeclarations` row — exactly as `split-section` gives its fresh suffix an explicit `newSectionMetadata` instead of a declaration keyed by an unallocated ID. Section 6.4's inference does not apply: this measure is not built from a parsed fragment, so its completion is declared, never inferred.

**Two new codes, not a reused one.** `edit-plan.duration-sum-mismatch` reports a mismatch between one event's declared spans; `edit-plan.measure-partition-mismatch` reports a mismatch between two measures' declared totals. Sharing the code would make them indistinguishable in a receipt. Each new code declares the accepted code it follows in the precedence order (`section-split-boundary-invalid` and `duration-sum-mismatch` respectively) rather than a number, so no accepted code is renumbered by the amendment.

**A split moves a bar line, never a beat.** Both totals are the caller's exact statement, recomputed from the stored durations and confirmed before any identity work. Nothing is computed for the caller, redistributed, rounded, or repaired. `beforeEventId` must be strict interior, so neither result is empty and the operation is never a no-op dressed as a split.

## Why it is additive rather than an edit

I first made the change in place, and TypeScript immediately listed the eight exhaustive switches in the runner, runtime-shape decoder, and bookmark mapper that a sixth variant breaks — plus `validate:a0-u1-edit-plan-contract` would have gone red on `planKinds` 5 vs 6, `lawRows` 17 vs 18, and the counts block. Landing the type without the runner, the 16k-line validator's twenty-odd per-kind oracles, and ~20 literal transitions would have left the aggregate gate red. That is not a stopping point.

So I reverted and used the packet's own idiom — the one that kept `ApplyEditPlanCommand` out of the live `DocumentCommand` union until its implementation leaf was claimed. The amendment lives in `src/application/application-split-measure-amendment-contract.ts`, re-exports the accepted declarations unchanged, and is imported by nothing in production. The build hash is byte-identical before and after (`94f8d417…`, 799,082 bytes), which is the proof that it is fully tree-shaken out.

## What was specified

- **`src/application/application-split-measure-amendment-contract.ts`** — the plan type, the proposed six-kind tuple and eighteen-law list, the two refusal codes with authority rows and precedence anchors, the exact-key authority, the `/plan/...` pointer templates, the allocated-identity shape, the id-allocation step and its anchor, the bookmark policy and its six-row boundary mapping, the completion-declaration accounting row, the transposition policy, the count delta, and the four claim flags — all false.
- **`docs/A0_U1_ATOMIC_EDIT_PLAN_CONTRACT.md` section 21** — the normative statement, appended as an amendment. Sections 1–20 are untouched: renumbering them would churn an accepted document and break its cross-references.
- **`docs/U1_EDITING_CONTRACT.md` section 5.3** — the deferral now names where the variant is specified and restates that U1 v1 still offers only Move, Shorten, or Cancel until the build leaf lands.
- **`tests/fixtures/editing/u1-editing-contract.json`** — the handoff row's `owner` moves from "a future A0/U1 amendment leaf" to the three real bead ids.

## The law-001 question

`A0-U1-ATOM-001-command-and-five-closed-variants` keeps its accepted identifier. A law named "five" describing a six-variant set is not ideal, but renaming it rewrites **109 references** across eight files including the 17 MB byte-pinned fixture whose R1 acceptance record cites those names. That is a change needing its own recorded acceptance, not a side effect of this amendment. The doc's section 21.6 states the closed set is six and why the identifier reads five, so no reader is misled. `A0_U1_SPLIT_MEASURE_LAW_001_RENAME_DEFERRED` records the decision in code.

## Evidence

- **`tests/static/a0-u1-split-measure-amendment.test.ts`** — 8 tests, 49 assertions. It proves the amendment is additive rather than an edit: the live sets are still 5 kinds / 32 codes / 17 laws, no added name collides with an accepted one, every accepted index still names its variant, the proposed sets are the accepted sets plus exactly the amendment, the allocation step sits between the event-level and section-level steps, each new code anchors to an accepted code, the plan value's own keys equal the declared authority, the completion accounting is internally exact, and the bookmark mapping moves only the two boundaries that denoted the source measure's end.
- `bun scripts/validate-a0-u1-edit-plan-contract.ts` — **pass, 0 findings**, with no `--allow-pending-freeze`. The accepted packet is untouched, which is the point.
- `bun scripts/validate-u1-contract.ts` — pass, 0 findings, 32/32 mutation controls replayed, digests re-pinned for the handoff edit.
- `bun test tests/static/` — 694 pass, 0 fail across 69 files.
- `bun run typecheck` clean; `bun run lint` pass, 144 files, 0 findings.
- `bun scripts/build.ts` — pass, hash and byte count unchanged from before the amendment.

## What the dependent leaves owe

**jcpe-pwp2 (build).** Move every declaration from the amendment module into `application-edit-plan-contract.ts`; then TypeScript names the sites: `targetFailure`, `completionDeclarationFailure`, `operationLawFailure`, `nonInsertPreparation`, `finalCollectionProjection`, `finalDurations`, and `materializePlan` in the runner — the last two have terminal `else` branches that currently assume `join-sections`, which is the riskiest silent-fallthrough site — plus `firstPlanShapeFailure` and `metadataWorkThroughPath` in the runtime-shape decoder, and the `switch (plan.kind)` plus a new `mapSplitMeasureBoundary` in the bookmark mapper. Then the U1 operation row for `split-at-bar` beside U1-OP-013, and `U1_AUTHORIZED_EDIT_PLAN_KINDS`.

**jcpe-tcm7 (verify).** Ten case groups (`A0U1-SPLITM-001…010`), roughly twenty literal transitions across apply/undo/redo/refusal/collision/plus-one with all seventeen `literalCatalog` companions each, one applicability row, one transposition witness, about five mutation controls, one trace, the eighteenth `lawCoverage` row, `EXPECTED_COUNTS` in the validator, the twenty-odd per-kind oracle branches, and both byte and semantic digests.

title: Concert Grand sounds tinny: needs warmth, body, and a real hall (owner listening feedback)
description: Owner: 'horrible and tinny, nothing like a warm Steinway in a concert hall'. MEASURED DIAGNOSIS (scratchpad tone-metrics + clip-probe over the real gain law): the DRY wasm render is NOT tinny (sustained centroid 150-320Hz, HF bands 50+dB down) — the damage is in the graph chain: at outputLevel 0.85, a 4-voice chord at velocity 96 hits the tanh(1.5x) soft-clip at pre-clip peak 0.61 producing ~5.1% THD+N (audible threshold ~0.1-0.5%) plus the curve's small-signal gain of 1.66 pushing levels further. FIX: (1) drop concert-grand outputLevel to ~0.40 so chord peaks stay <0.3 into the shaper (THD ~0.5%), recover loudness at master-gain (it sits AFTER the clipper); consider normalizing the curve to unity small-signal gain; (2) hall: reverb send 0.2*0.28=0.056 into a 2s noise burst is no concert hall — author a longer (3.5-4s) exponentially-decaying lowpass-colored deterministic impulse (xorshift, re-pin impulse-golden.json + hashes) and raise default reverbAmount ~0.35; (3) optional warmth: hammer corner 800+8000v^1.6 -> ~500+2600v^1.6, small 2nd/3rd partial boost. VERIFY numerically (THD<0.6%, centroid targets, band balance) then redeploy for owner listening. Metric scripts preserved in the session scratchpad pattern; rebuild them from the bead text if gone.

title: Live groove switch: changing the groove during playback re-performs the running plan immediately
description: Today the groove picker states 'Groove applies on the next Play' — changing ballad→swing mid-playback does nothing until Stop/Play. Required: the running transport re-performs instantly (within one scheduler lookahead window) when the groove changes, without stopping, losing the playhead position, or glitching sounding voices. Mechanism precedent: V2R-16 fader ride (studio-live-mix) already carries a committed parameter into the live engine mid-run; grooves are heavier because the performed plan (compilePerformancePlan over the immutable playback plan) must be recompiled and swapped at a bar/beat boundary through the serialized X1 transport command lane — audio consumes plans/serialized commands only, never UI state. Laws to specify before build: swap boundary (next beat vs next bar — pick one, state it), what happens to already-scheduled lookahead events (cancel-and-reschedule from the boundary), undo semantics unchanged (setPerformanceStyle stays one undoable settings command; the live swap is a playback effect, not a second history entry), and refusal path (if the re-perform refuses, playback continues on the old plan and the surface says so). TESTS + LOGGING: unit tests over the swap planner (boundary math, plan identity, cancel set) with machine-readable dumps; X1-style transport witness test proving command serialization ordering; x0/studio-audible e2e that renders audio while switching groove mid-bar and asserts (a) no dropout/overlap via the offline-render harness, (b) the post-switch bars match the new groove's performed plan, with the render-and-compare metrics written to test-results/. Same law applies to the instrument/voice switch bead (jcpe: see live-instrument bead) — share the swap machinery.
notes: CONTROLLER+UI LANE COMPLETE (LilacHorizon), joining the fork's transport lane: rideLivePerformance in studio-controller.ts recompiles + re-performs under the new style and sends port.setPerformance with the post-commit revision, then re-stamps activeRun so later seek/loop rebinds stay alive; wired after every successful setPerformanceStyle; 'Groove applies on the next Play.' copy replaced with 'The groove changes right away, from the next chord.' Tests: tests/unit/studio-live-performance-ride.test.ts — mid-run swap bumps the transport generation while status stays playing and a subsequent seek succeeds (the stale-revision trap), one-undo law preserved, no-run changes never touch the transport. Gates green: typecheck 0, eslint clean, validate:x1-contract 0 findings (119 cells), 21/21 across the five transport suites, build green (4,827,569 bytes). REMAINING before close: the x0/studio-audible offline-render e2e named in this bead (groove switch mid-bar, no dropout, post-switch bars match the new groove) — requires the Playwright audible config and must chain behind the currently running suite.

title: U1 spec packet: four interaction cases and five refusal codes have no reachable production state
description:
Recorded by U1/verify (jcpe-milestone-reliable-studio-l3a.10.3) after driving 59 of 59 operation-matrix rows and 54 of 58 interaction cases. Neither item is a U1 production defect; both are packet questions for the spec author.

## Four interaction cases with no reachable state

- U1-INT-002 ('playback advances across three chords') and U1-INT-003 ('a chord preview is auditioned from the card menu') need playback and audition. The studio transport reports status 'unavailable', isAvailable false: X0/X1 are not wired to it. Blocked on U4/X1, not on U1.
- U1-INT-006 states its precondition as 'playhead at beat 12'. No U1 operation may move the playhead (that is the law it tests) and nothing else can until the transport is wired. Its three-bookmark half is asserted by U1-INT-005; its rendered-accessible-name half is not, so the case is deliberately left unlinked rather than half-claimed.
- U1-INT-026 ('the chart region is unmounted') has no product path: StudioShell mounts ChartWorkspace unconditionally for the lifetime of the app. The leak class it guards is covered instead by U1-INT-020 (a card unmounted mid-drag) and U1-INT-023 (per-card listener totals across ten reorders).

Either the three transport-dependent cases are re-linked once U4/X1 land, or U1-INT-006 is restated so its bookmark half can be claimed on its own; U1-INT-026 needs a reachable precondition or an explicit note that it is a design constraint rather than a testable state.

## Five declared refusal codes with no production site

U1_REFUSAL_CODES declares 29; production implements 24.

- u1.preview_token_limit - no draft in the reviewed corpus reaches the 2,048-token preview bound.
- u1.duration_underfills_measure_requires_reason - production uses the also-declared u1.completion_reason_required for exactly this state.
- u1.stale_revision - production uses the more precise u1.quick_entry_stale_revision, and no other gesture captures a revision that could go stale: every other command reads the live snapshot at dispatch.
- u1.pointer_capture_lost and u1.operation_not_authorized - both describe states the surface reaches without needing to name a code. Both are now driven behaviourally (U1-OPC-056, U1-OPC-053).

Either the inventory narrows to the codes a gesture can actually produce, or the contract states which of the five are reserved for a later package.
close_reason:
Both halves are resolved, and the investigation turned up one thing the bead had wrong: the five refusal codes were not all dead names. One of them guarded a reachable state production was not guarding.

## The production defect behind `u1.preview_token_limit`

The bead recorded "no draft in the reviewed corpus reaches the 2,048-token preview bound." True of the corpus, false of the product. **2,048 undurated chords are 4,095 code points — one inside the draft bound.** T0 refuses that draft and publishes all 2,048 as recoverable chords. The preview emitted recovered chords first and diagnostics second, both against one shared budget, so the sole diagnostic row fell off the end:

```
before: rows=2048 {"insertable":2048}              diagnosticRowsPresent=false
after:  rows=2048 {"insertable":2047,"invalid":1}  diagnosticRowsPresent=true
```

A refused draft rendered as nothing but a list of chords to insert, with no stated reason — a refusal presented as a success, which section 6 of the contract forbids outright. The code declared for exactly this state was never emitted.

Fixed in `previewQuickEntryDraft`: room for every T0 diagnostic is reserved before any recovered chord is listed, so a rendering bound can never drop the row that says why the draft refused. The shortfall is now stated rather than silently absent — `StudioDraftPreview.truncation` carries the code, the shown and total row counts, and a sentence; `App.tsx` maps it to `truncationNotice` and `LibraryPanel` renders it under the token list. `u1.preview_token_limit` stays in the inventory because it now names something.

Two regression tests in `tests/integration/u1-refusal-rows.test.ts` drive both sides: the 4,095-code-point/2,048-chord draft keeps its diagnostic row and states the shortfall; the 1,024-chord draft at the same code-point count sits inside the bound, shows all 1,025 rows, and claims no truncation.

## The other four codes: inventory narrowed 29 -> 25

Each names a pre-dispatch refusal that no gesture can produce, and in three cases a reviewed matrix row asserted the surface produces it.

| Removed | Why no gesture reaches it |
|---|---|
| `u1.duration_underfills_measure_requires_reason` | a second name for the state `u1.completion_reason_required` already names |
| `u1.stale_revision` | only quick entry captures a revision, and it refuses with the precise `u1.quick_entry_stale_revision`; every other gesture reads the live snapshot at dispatch |
| `u1.pointer_capture_lost` | losing capture mid-drag is a cancellation, not a refusal: capture is released, transient listeners are removed, nothing is dispatched |
| `u1.operation_not_authorized` | the six unauthorized command kinds have no U1 control at all, so there is no gesture to refuse |

`U1-OPC-034`, `U1-OPC-053` and `U1-OPC-056` now carry `refusalCode: null` with notes stating what the surface actually does. Their behaviour was already proven — only the declared code was fictional.

**The inventory is now self-policing.** A new static test walks `src/` and requires every declared refusal code to appear somewhere other than the inventory that declares it. A code with no production site fails the gate instead of sitting in a closed list looking like a guard.

## Four unreachable states: declared, and checked

Rather than dropping the four cases or leaving 54-of-58 unexplained, `reachability` becomes a declared field on any interaction or operation row the product cannot enter, with `state: "blocked"` plus the owning package, or `state: "unreachable-by-design"` plus the constraint. Both owe a written reason; the validator rejects a malformed record, a missing reason, a blocked row naming no package, and an unreachable row naming one.

- **U1-INT-002** blocked by **X1** — the transport reports `unavailable`/`isAvailable false`, so no gesture can advance a playhead to observe the selection against.
- **U1-INT-003** blocked by **U2** — auditioning one chord is a U2 preview control over the X0 engine; U1 declares no audition gesture.
- **U1-INT-006** blocked by **X1** — its stated precondition is "playhead at beat 12". The three-bookmark half is proven independently by U1-INT-005; the fourth value and the four-way rendered-name claim wait on the transport.
- **U1-INT-026** unreachable by design — and the impossibility is now *measured*, not asserted: a static test proves `StudioShell` mounts `ChartWorkspace` exactly once, unconditionally, inside the workspace landmark, with no conditional operator, logical guard, or null branch gating it.
- **U1-OPC-034** unreachable by design — no gesture outside quick entry captures a revision that can go stale; the existing test measures that the Delete which does run is the correct one against current state.

Three new ledger rules keep this honest, and one of them caught me mid-change:

1. **every undriven row declares why** — a row with neither evidence nor a stated reason fails;
2. **no blocked row is quietly already driven** — once X1/U2 land and something drives the row, the stale deferral fails rather than lingering;
3. **every unreachable-by-design row has a test that measures it** — "cannot happen" is otherwise indistinguishable from "was never tried". This rule is why U1-INT-026 got a real proof instead of a sentence.

## Gates

- `bun scripts/validate-u1-contract.ts` — **pass**, 0 findings, 32 of 32 mutation controls replayed, no `--allow-pending-freeze`.
- `bun test` — **2,429 pass, 0 fail across 223 files**, no skips, retries, or quarantine.
- `bun test tests/static/` re-run after the rebuild — 686 pass, 0 fail across 68 files.
- `bun run typecheck` clean. `bun run lint` pass, 143 files, 0 findings.
- `bun scripts/build.ts` — pass, 799,082 bytes, hash `94f8d417e77ff36ccb747b5d84483e726ef4f2655b05f2d5fba3714332ef0a18`, root and `dist` regenerated from source.

Re-pinned: `edit-operation-matrix.json` 7a679ad44183a67f6c2d2ecb4fee941df9584e30eddfa63d02f0366c924dfa51, `interaction-state-matrix.json` 4a8fd91eb5c23f6e3f8d8a9ab03c95b4c4a0bff391f5c7eb606fbbc54adbd9ba, semantic ed7795ff9a3667125da25f0a6689622304f4063e55e1b31e8a76cdbec5058a91.

Contract updated: section 6 states the reserved-diagnostic-row rule and the four removals with reasons; new section 6.1 defines `reachability`.

Note for whoever lands **U4/X1** and **U2**: ledger rule 2 will fail the moment you drive U1-INT-002, 003 or 006. That failure is the signal to delete the `reachability` record from the row, not to relax the rule.

title: Clarinet v2: high+soft cells are pure noise (no phonation); loud cells carry background hiss
description:
OWNER LISTENING VERDICTS (2026-08-06, pack eb688080f82197dd, verbatim): high-soft-tongued-candidate.wav "sounds like pure noise"; high-soft-legato-candidate.wav "so does this" (pure noise); high-loud-tongued-candidate.wav "sounds pretty good"; high-loud-legato-candidate.wav "also sounds good but with some high frequency noise"; middle-loud-tongued-candidate.wav and middle-loud-legato-candidate.wav "also sound pretty good except noisy, like background noise hiss".

Diagnosis to verify by measurement before fixing (measure-the-sound law):
CLASS 1 — no phonation at high+soft: MIDI 74 velocity 36 produces turbulence only, both articulations. Expected mechanism: the velocity->breath-pressure mapping drops below the reed oscillation threshold, which RISES with register (shorter tube = less feedback gain). Playbook plateau law: clarinet speaks at breath 0.68-0.88; dynamics must be expressed WITHIN the speaking plateau (reduced pressure near the lower plateau edge + output gain + darker spectrum), never by pushing the exciter sub-threshold. Fix direction: register-aware pressure floor (or threshold-referenced pressure mapping p = p_threshold(register) + dynamics*(headroom)), never a silent gain hack. Prove with a phonation sweep: every (register x velocity 1..127) cell must achieve pitch lock (autocorrelation f0 within +-8c) with HNR above an authored floor.
CLASS 2 — background hiss on otherwise-good cells (middle-loud both, high-loud-legato HF noise): v2 turbulence likely exceeds the measured noise laws (in-loop turbulence 0.004-0.009, radiated one-pole band-limit ~5.5 kHz, direct injection <= 0.01; radiation differentiator adds +6 dB/oct — band-limit radiated fields). Measure HNR of the failing cells vs the shipped v1 (v1 measured 31-37 dB); v2 must meet or beat v1 or the row stays red.

Constraints: coordinate with jcpe-mnsc.4.3 (PHS2/verify, in_progress) — a red listening row blocks green verify (plan section 13.4: failed row stays red until implementation amended and RE-AUDITIONED). All existing v2 gates must stay green after the fix (tuning fixture incl. clarinet@2 rows, alias suite clarinet@2 rows, chiff tests, waveguide-renderer, parameter-pack table checks). Wasm regen + full re-pin sweep. Regenerate the listening pack (scripts/render-phs2-listening-pack.ts) for OWNER re-audition — never self-author the listening verdict; the deliverable ends at "new pack ready for ears".
close_reason: Both defect classes fixed, measured, and gated; owner re-audition is the remaining gate. CLASS 1 (no phonation): v2's velocity->pressure mapping (legacy 0.68+0.20*v^1.3) sat below the segmented lattice's register-dependent oscillation threshold; measured the speaking band per register by autocorrelation pitch-lock scan (phonation is an INTERVAL - overblowing closes the reed), mapped dynamics into the band interior (10 anchors, 25% floor, fork-fingering pocket 66-67 anchored separately after a finer sweep caught wrong-mode locks). CLASS 2 (hiss): v2-scoped noise laws - in-loop turbulence 0.004+0.005v (lower half of playbook band), direct bleed 0.012->0.009, hole/vent radiation corners capped 5.5 kHz (were 7 kHz); v2 HNR now >= v1 in EVERY cell (before: ~2 dB below everywhere; after: 39.0 vs 29.9 low-soft, 57.3 vs unphonated high-soft, 58.3 vs 56.2 high-loud). Tuning recalibrated at the new operating points (band_pocket -6c 68-77, altissimo_top -5c at 89, clarion_top 96k rate term; residuals <=5.5c all rates all registers). Fork pocket joined the 2x oversample regime (alias fixture 66@44.1k was 4 dB over comparative; now below its own 96k baseline). v1 legacy proven BYTE-IDENTICAL (aggregate sha e7e27db7 over 48 cells, HEAD wasm vs new wasm). New permanent gates: tests/unit/clarinet-v2-phonation.test.ts (154 cells x pitch-lock+HNR floor + detector known-answer controls incl. the exact noise class the owner heard) and scripts/listening-screen.ts pre-listening screen wired into the pack generator (5 known-answer controls in tests/unit/listening-screen.test.ts; SCREEN-FAILED cells mark the manifest and exit nonzero - human listening is never again spent on machine-detectable noise). Gates: cargo 24/24; bun 104/104 across 11 suites + 10/10 pack/screen/phonation; typecheck clean; eslint clean. NEW PACK FOR OWNER RE-AUDITION: test-results/clarinet-v2-listening/533abbdd277b2911 (12 cells, 0 screen failures, references included). No commits; listening verdict NOT claimed.

title: Predeploy flute@2 evidence replay fails: document and require the UIowa reference corpus
description:

(tests/unit/uiowa-clarinet-reference.test.ts) and "ledger evaluation fails closed > flute@2 requires exact replay..." (tests/unit/check-predeploy.test.ts:277, expected "pass", received "unavailable"). Verified 2026-09-01: 3853 pass / 2 fail, twice reproduced. This violates the Release Definition of Done requirement that all commands pass from a clean checkout, and it makes gate outcomes depend on undocumented machine-local state.

Why: fail-closed on missing reference audio is correct policy (third-party recordings cannot be committed); the defect is that the requirement is invisible. An agent or fresh machine cannot distinguish "evidence rotted" from "corpus not installed".

Do NOT weaken fail-closed behavior, skip the tests, or mark them conditional.

Approach: (1) Run `bun scripts/build-dsp.ts --check` now (requires the pinned rust toolchain — record the exact rustc/wasm-opt versions the last pin used: rustc 1.99.0-nightly 1a98b1e13 2026-08-07, wasm-opt 131 -Oz) and record whether drift exists today. If cargo cannot be a verify-time dependency (Bun-only build contract), implement the guard as a source-hash ledger: record the sha256 of every dsp/ source file at pin time in the generated module and have a bun-only gate compare — no cargo needed at verify time.

Acceptance: a deliberate one-line change to any dsp/concert-grand/src file that feeds the payload turns a named gate red without running cargo at verify time (or with cargo, if that route is chosen and documented); current drift status is resolved and recorded with exact hashes; DEPLOY_GATE.md documents the guard. title: ABI-v2 validates f64 state ranges at only 4-byte alignment
description:
Audit finding (2026-08-06). ABI-v2 validation under-checks alignment: state regions hold f64 by the ABI's own convention but are validated only to 4-byte alignment, so a "validated" request can still make the host throw.

Evidence: dsp/concert-grand/src/physical.rs:134 enforces `start % 4 != 0` for all ranges, while `state_output`/`state_input` for phs_modal_render_v2 are f64 arrays. An 8-byte-misaligned offset passes validation, then a host-side Float64Array view on wasm memory throws RangeError — precisely the class of failure phs_validate_v2 claims to have excluded (PHS0 contract section 6: validate each range BEFORE access; malformed requests must not trap the host).

Fix: enforce 8-byte alignment for every f64-bearing range (state input/output, and any future control arrays declared f64 — audit each descriptor's element type and validate accordingly). Add the alignment rule to the contract text and the fixture packet.

Acceptance:
- Near-miss fixtures: state offset = 4 mod 8 refuses with the named alignment code (Rust unit test AND host-side test through dsp-renderer.ts hitting real wasm memory).
- Positive: aligned request unchanged.
- Mutation: dropping the 8-byte check is caught.
- cargo + bun test green; conformance fixture counts re-pinned (coordinate with peer's in-flight jcpe-mnsc.2.3 test files — tests/unit/physical-abi.test.ts is peer-dirty; wait or coordinate).
close_reason: 8-byte alignment now enforced for f64-bearing state ranges: ByteRange::checked gained a per-region alignment parameter (4 for i32/f32 regions, 8 for state input/output), raw-pointer alignment checks added to phs_modal_render_v2 (4-byte PCM, 8-byte state/energy pointers) and phs_reed_solve_v2 (8-byte output) since misaligned slices are UB. Host bug fixed in the same class: dsp-renderer.ts statePointer was rightPointer+channelBytes which is 4 mod 8 for odd frame counts, making the Float64Array state view throw before any wasm validation - now aligned up to 8, with regression test at frameCount=255. Host near-miss coverage in NEW file tests/unit/physical-abi-alignment.test.ts (peer-dirty tests/unit/physical-abi.test.ts untouched per coordination constraint): state offsets at 4 mod 8 refuse with physical.abi_bounds_invalid, 8-aligned accepts, existing fixture near-miss offset 1 still refuses. Rust near-miss test rejects_f64_state_ranges_that_are_only_four_aligned (initial fixture accidentally aliased the request blob at offset 16/20; moved to disjoint 16384/16388 - aliasing refusal is a different named check). Commands: RCH_CARGO_WRAPPER_BYPASS=1 cargo test -> 16 passed 0 failed; bun scripts/build-dsp.ts -> wasm 39471 bytes sha256=c786e935...; bun --bun test physical-abi-alignment/physical-modal/physical-nonlinear/waveguide-renderer -> 18 pass 0 fail; bun scripts/validate-phs0-contract.ts -> findings []. description:
Audit finding (2026-08-06). Every nonlinearity in the live models runs at base rate with zero oversampling, and alias energy is unmeasured and unbounded by any fixture. The plan makes the oversampling decision explicit only for trumpet; the same law must cover what already ships.

Evidence: guitar amp `tanh(asym*drive)` plus squared asymmetry term at base rate (dsp/concert-grand/src/guitar.rs:409); clarinet reed table clamp (clarinet.rs), flute cubic jet (flute.rs), winds.rs clamps likewise. At drive 1.25-1.55 aliasing is mild but real, worst at 44.1 kHz with bright twang settings. docs/PHYSICAL_SYNTHESIS_PLAN.md sections 10.1/11.1 require the alias decision to be explicit and MEASURED.

Work:
1. Add an alias-energy metric to the existing analyzer/render-harness toolkit (scratchpad model-measure.ts patterns; see the groove-campaign-playbook memory for harness locations): render a high tessitura note at 44.1k and 96k, measure energy at known alias-image frequencies of the top partials (inharmonic images that fold below Nyquist), report dB relative to signal.
2. Author independent thresholds per instrument (literature/listening-derived, not production-derived).
3. Where a model exceeds threshold, implement minimal mitigation: 2x oversample just the amp/nonlinear stage with half-band filters, or reduce drive headroom — measured, not assumed. Keep the decision per component and record it.
4. Wire the metric into the evidence suite so future models (trumpet PHS5) inherit it.

Acceptance:
- Metric has a known-answer synthetic control (a deliberately aliased hard-clip must score high; a band-limited signal near zero).
- Measured alias tables for guitar (both profiles), flute, clarinet at 44.1/48/96 kHz recorded in evidence output.
- Any mitigation keeps tuning/HNR/brightness within existing measured bounds (re-run the model-measure sweep) and re-pins hashes via the count-authority sweep.
close_reason: Independent alias-energy fixture landed as tests/unit/physical-alias-energy.test.ts (Goertzel tonal-excess extractor sharing no code with the crate FFT/analyzer/harness). Known-answer controls: hard-clipped ~988 Hz sine scores > -45 dBc total (PASS high), band-limited additive < -70 dBc (PASS floor), and a comparative control proves the tier-2 law flags genuine 44.1k aliasing against a 96k baseline (>3 dB mean-excess gap). Authored two-tier law: absolute -50 dBc, else per-image mean excess within +3 dB of the instrument's own 96 kHz noise-only baseline (fold sources >=48 kHz are dead in these band-limited loops). MEASURED TABLE (velocity 120, sustain 0.15-0.50 s, chiff/vibrato excluded): guitar-clean midi64 -80.0/-74.6/-86.8 dBc total at 44.1/48/96k, midi84 -93.8/-93.6/-107.5; guitar-drive midi64 -68.5/-72.7/-84.3, midi84 -82.3/-94.3/-110.3; flute midi72 -36.4/-38.8/-34.1 (noise-floor-limited, comparative pass: mean/image -46.8/-48.8 vs baseline -47.1), midi89 comparative pass; clarinet midi66 -50.1/-49.5 vs baseline -56.7 comparative pass, midi87 -57.4/-55.7 tier-1 pass. DECISION per component: NO oversampling mitigation required at current drive levels - guitar worst true-alias cell (-68.5 dBc) is 18 dB inside the audibility gate; wind fold-back is undetectable above the authored turbulence bed. Metric is wired into the evidence suite (future models append to the cases array; trumpet PHS5 inherits it). No Rust changed, so no re-pin/tuning re-run owed. title: No denormal protection in DSP crate (determinism + tail stalls)
description:
Audit finding (2026-08-06). No denormal protection anywhere in the DSP crate — a determinism AND performance defect (plan section 6.5 requires protection).

Evidence: every renderer carries exponentially decaying f64 state: OnePoleLoss.state and DC blockers (dsp/concert-grand/src/physical.rs), env_fast/env_slow (lib.rs:346-347), guitar loop samples and body modes (guitar.rs), wind bores (clarinet.rs/flute.rs). WASM mandates gradual underflow (no FTZ available), and denormal multiplies stall 10-100x on common x86 engines. Long tails (8 s bass piano notes, guitar T60 paths) walk straight through the denormal range, so render cost spikes exactly on the notes that are already the most expensive.

Fix: deterministic threshold flush at the few persistent state points: after each state update, if |x| < 1e-20 set to 0.0 (or add/subtract a constant 1e-18 offset inside loss filters — choose flush, it is simpler to reason about and test). Audibly nothing (state is ~-400 dB); numerically deterministic on every host. Apply to: one-pole loss filters, DC blockers, envelope followers, waveguide loop samples at the loss point, body/formant mode states, complex-rotation piano oscillators (flush the pair magnitude). Do NOT rely on platform FTZ flags.

Also (same loops, same rebuild): early-out the render when total remaining energy falls below the existing trailing-trim threshold — today the renderer computes the full capacity even after the note is inaudible, so tail seconds of oscillator math are pure waste (lib.rs render loops trim STORED frames, not COMPUTED frames).

Acceptance:
- Unit test (Rust): drive a loss filter with an impulse for 10 s of samples; assert no state value is ever subnormal (f64::is_subnormal) across all renderers' state probes.
- Determinism: render hashes identical across two runs; re-pin pinned hashes once (flush changes late-tail bits) via the count-authority sweep.
- Perf evidence: measured render time for a low piano note before/after recorded in the close reason (expect the early-out to dominate the win).
- cargo test + full bun test + wasm hash re-pin sweep.
close_reason: Deterministic flush_denormal (|x|<1e-20 -> 0) added at every decaying state: OnePoleLoss/DcBlocker (physical.rs), guitar Allpass/Mode ticks + loop loss point + click/sag/pre-hp/cab-hp envelopes (guitar.rs), piano noise/thump/oscillator envelopes at a 256-frame checkpoint that also computes a monotone output bound and early-outs (zero-fills) the inaudible tail after the 0.2s normalization window (lib.rs). No FTZ flags used. Tests: cargo test 19/19 (new: decaying_component_states_never_go_subnormal, flush_denormal_is_identity_above_threshold_and_zero_below, long_bass_render_contains_no_subnormal_or_nonfinite_samples); bun --bun test on waveguide-renderer, concert-grand-renderer, piano-hybrid, dsp-analysis, physical-modal, physical-nonlinear, physical-abi-alignment = 44 pass/0 fail. Determinism double-render tests green. Perf (median of 9, same machine): piano-24-v100-96k 88.16->80.67ms, piano-24-v30-96k 84.40->75.19ms, piano-48-v100-48k 51.45->47.94ms, guitar-40-v100-48k 28.00->19.68ms (-30%), flute unchanged 9.3->9.6ms. Wasm regenerated via scripts/build-dsp.ts, sha 337e7f25...ffb6fe1c8, 40275 bytes; no PCM hash pins exist in non-peer test files (verified by search), module sha auto-updates in generated concert-grand-wasm.ts. Flush is below f32 audibility so trim counts and measured behavior unchanged.

title: ABI-v2 energy ledger residual is vacuous (only detects growth)
description:
Audit finding (2026-08-06, Rust DSP auditor). The ABI-v2 energy ledger is vacuous: the residual is defined to be zero whenever energy decreased, so the audit can only ever detect energy GROWTH, never mis-accounted loss, radiation, or collision terms.

Evidence: dsp/concert-grand/src/physical.rs:342-350 computes `dissipated = (excited_energy - final_energy).max(0.0)` and then `ledger[3] = excited_energy - final_energy - dissipated` — algebraically zero for any passive run. The test at physical.rs:580 asserting `ledger[3].abs() < 1e-12` therefore proves nothing. This contradicts docs/PHYSICAL_SYNTHESIS_PLAN.md section 6.2 (independent per-block accounting of exciter input, stored energy, radiated output, damping loss, collision loss, residual) and PHS0 contract section 7.

Fix: compute each dissipation channel INDEPENDENTLY from its component state (e.g. loss filter absorption = sum over samples of the energy removed by the loss coefficient; radiation = energy of the radiated output samples; collision loss from the contact model when it exists), then report residual = input - stored - radiated - losses as a genuinely independent closure check. Set per-model, per-sample-rate residual tolerances authored in the fixture packet (not derived from production output). Update the conformance test to include a NEAR-MISS: a deliberately active coefficient (loss gain > 1) must produce a nonzero residual/refusal — the mutation the current ledger cannot catch.

Acceptance:
- Positive: passive modal render residual within authored tolerance, with dissipation terms individually nonzero and plausible.
- Near-miss: active coefficient run flagged (nonzero residual beyond tolerance or named refusal).
- Mutation: zeroing any single ledger term breaks its named assertion.
- cargo test in dsp/concert-grand green; wasm rebuilt via scripts/build-dsp.ts with hash re-pin; bun test suites that pin the wasm hash updated (count-authority re-pin sweep per the sampled-instruments landing checklist).
close_reason: Implemented independent per-sample damping-loss accumulation (Kahan) in modal_core; ledger now 6 slots [initial, work, final, dampingLoss, residual, limiter] with residual a genuine closure check. Near-miss test energy_ledger_flags_an_active_coefficient proves loss>1 is visible (negative damping term, energy growth) — the mutation the old ledger could not catch; positive tests recompute closure independently in both Rust and TS. Commands: RCH_CARGO_WRAPPER_BYPASS=1 cargo test (dsp/concert-grand) -> 11 passed 0 failed; bun scripts/build-dsp.ts -> wasm 39215 bytes sha256=89aaf9cc...; /home/ubuntu/.bun/bin/bun --bun test tests/unit/physical-modal.test.ts tests/unit/physical-nonlinear.test.ts tests/unit/waveguide-renderer.test.ts -> 14 pass 0 fail (v1 render pins untouched, proving v1 byte-identity); bun scripts/validate-phs0-contract.ts -> findings []. title: Flute MIDI 93/96 at 44.1/48 kHz: sub-14-sample jets refuse fractional tuning (regime flips)
description: Found and scoped 2026-08-06 by the independent autocorrelation tuning fixture (tests/unit/physical-tuning-independent.test.ts) during jcpe-dsp-tuning-independent-6fyy. The flute jet delay is period/2 samples; the truncation deficit was measured to pull notes sharp by ~692*d/period cents. A fractional-delay allpass in the jet path, with its coefficient solved for exact phase delay AT f0 (48-step bisection), fixed the whole register at all three rates EXCEPT jets under ~14 samples: flute MIDI 93/96 at 44.1/48 kHz flip oscillation regime (+-75..90 cents) with any allpass in the jet loop. Those four cells now bypass the fractional jet (a=0 pure-delay topology, exactly the shipped truncated jet) and keep their shipped residuals: 48k 93:+16.7 96:+14.8; 44.1k 93:+17.1 96:-46.5 (C7 regime outlier). Post-fix everywhere else: 44.1k max |2.2|c through MIDI 90, 48k max |1.8|, 96k max |4.4| across 60..96. The fixture excludes exactly these four cells with a comment naming this bead. Fix directions: jet nonlinearity is phase-sensitive at short delays - consider oversampling the jet path at 44.1/48k for MIDI >= 93, a different fractional structure (Lagrange FIR has flat phase but adds damping), or accept until PHS3 flute-v2 (fingering-dependent bore sections + tone-hole lattice) replaces this model. Prove by removing the fixture exclusions.

title: Bit-identical DSP hot-loop optimizations (modulo, zeroing, secant)
description:
Performance cleanups (2026-08-06 audit) that are BIT-IDENTICAL by construction — no hash re-pin, no retuning, pure speed. Keep strictly separate from any change that alters sample math.

Items (all in dsp/concert-grand/src):
1. DelayLine::push integer modulo per sample (physical.rs:93) and guitar's `(write + 1) % length` (guitar.rs:380), same pattern in winds.rs:267 when it lands -> compare-and-reset (`w += 1; if w == len { w = 0 }`). Integer division every sample per line is the single hottest scalar op in the waveguide loops.
2. Redundant residual evaluation in the reed solver secant loop (physical.rs:449-456 recomputes high_residual when high did not move) -> cache it. (Coordinate with the reed-solver-budget bead if both are open; land order does not matter but do not double-edit.)
3. Per-note buffer zeroing writes the full backing slice even for short bores (DelayLine::new at physical.rs:77 zeroes all of `storage`; flute zeroes 2x8192 f64 = 128 KB for a ~200-sample bore) -> zero only `length` slots.
4. Verify with wasm-oriented profiling (bun-side wall-clock over N renders is fine as evidence; per profiling-software-performance discipline: measure before AND after, same machine, recorded in the close reason).

Explicitly out of scope: LFO rotation recurrence (rides with dsp-vibrato-variation because it changes bits), opt-level/SIMD build flags (separate evaluation bead), denormal flush (separate bead, changes bits).

Acceptance:
- Render hashes byte-identical to pre-change output for every instrument at all three sample rates (this is the whole point — prove it with the existing hash pins, no re-pin allowed).
- Measured cold-render time improvement recorded (expect modest single-digit to ~20% on waveguide-heavy notes).
- cargo test + full bun test green; wasm rebuilt (byte-identical wasm is NOT expected — only identical RENDER OUTPUT; the embedded wasm hash pin still needs its routine update via scripts/build-dsp.ts).
close_reason: Bit-identical hot-loop cleanups: DelayLine::push modulo -> compare-and-reset and DelayLine::new zeroes only the active window (physical.rs); guitar polarization write advance and bridge-slot index modulo -> compare-based (guitar.rs); reed solver caches endpoint residuals so the unchanged endpoint is never re-evaluated (physical.rs secant loop; halves function evaluations per iteration, numerically identical since reed_residual is pure). Byte-identity PROVEN: 21-case render-hash witness (piano 24/60/96 x v100/64, guitar clean+drive, flute, clarinet at 44.1/48/96k) identical before/after (scratchpad hashes-before/after diff empty). cargo test 19/19; bun --bun test waveguide/physical-modal/physical-nonlinear/physical-abi-alignment/concert-grand suites 25/25. Perf medians (9 runs): piano-24-v100-96k 80.67->76.41ms, guitar-40 19.68->19.39ms, flute 9.55->9.57ms - modest, as the denormal bead had already removed the dominant stalls; the win is structural (no per-sample integer division remains in any waveguide loop). Wasm regenerated, sha 7960f31c...17119eb (40537 bytes); render output unchanged, module sha auto-updated in generated file. winds.rs untouched: tracked but not compiled into lib.rs (no mod declaration), so edits there would be unverifiable dead code.

title: ABI-v2 limiter rescales output block but not handed-off state
description:
Audit finding (2026-08-06). The ABI-v2 safety limiter rescales the output block but not the handed-off state, guaranteeing a level step at the next block boundary.

Evidence: dsp/concert-grand/src/physical.rs:332-341 rescales the whole block when peak > 0.98, but lines 344-345 hand off oscillator state (x, y) unscaled. A caller continuing the next block from that state resumes at pre-limit amplitude: audible click/step exactly at the block seam. Also ambiguous against PHS0 section 7 (limiter is protection, never musical normalization; engagement counted).

Fix (choose one, document in the contract): (a) declare the limiter OUTPUT-ONLY — state hand-off stays physical/unscaled, ledger records engagement (it partly does via ledger[4]) and the receipt reports it, and the HOST must not stitch limited blocks as if continuous; or (b) scale state consistently with output so continuation is seamless but the stored energy record must then reflect the removed energy. Option (a) is more honest physics (the limiter is a safety valve, not part of the model); pick (b) only if block-stitched streaming is the intended v2 usage. Whichever is chosen, add the block-boundary continuity semantics to docs/PHS0_PHYSICAL_RENDERER_CONTRACT.md.

Acceptance:
- Test rendering a deliberately hot two-block sequence: under (a) the receipt flags engagement on block 1 and the contract text defines stitching as invalid; under (b) block 2 continues without a discontinuity exceeding an authored epsilon at the seam.
- Mutation: removing the chosen consistency rule breaks its named assertion.
- cargo test green; wasm hash re-pin sweep if bytes change.
close_reason: Option (a) adopted: limiter is OUTPUT-ONLY. Documented in docs/PHS0_PHYSICAL_RENDERER_CONTRACT.md section 7 (block-boundary stitching semantics: stitching a limited block against its continuation is invalid; receipt engagement count is the consultable evidence) and as a code comment at the limiter in phs_modal_render_v2. New Rust test limiter_is_output_only_and_state_hands_off_physically proves: block one engages (ledger[5]=1), published peak <= 0.98, handed-off state implies amplitude above ceiling (physical, unscaled), continuation state bit-identical to unlimited whole render. Commands: RCH_CARGO_WRAPPER_BYPASS=1 cargo test physical -> 6 passed; bun scripts/build-dsp.ts --check -> zero drift (test-only Rust change, wasm payload unchanged). Files: dsp/concert-grand/src/physical.rs (test + comment landed with bead 1 refactor), docs/PHS0_PHYSICAL_RENDERER_CONTRACT.md.

title: Reed solver tolerance unreachable in frozen iteration budget
description:
Audit finding (2026-08-06). The ABI-v2 reed solver's convergence tolerance is unreachable within its frozen iteration budget, so physically valid inputs are refused as nonconvergent.

Evidence: dsp/concert-grand/src/physical.rs:428 sets tolerance `1e-10*(1+|pm|+|pb|)` on the residual, but the fallback (physical.rs:441-496) is only 16 bisections over a bracket of O(1) width (mouth-bore), reaching interval ~1.5e-5 — residual ~1e-5 with O(1) slope, five orders above tolerance. The secant phase can stall near the aperture kink of `reed_flow` (physical.rs:358, `max(0.0)` introduces a derivative discontinuity), after which the bisection budget cannot recover, and the function returns 0 = refusal for ordinary playing pressures. PHS0 freezes eight primary iterations + sixteen fallback bisections (contract section 7), so the BUDGET is law; the TOLERANCE must be what that budget honestly achieves.

Fix: set the acceptance tolerance to the certified worst-case interval the 8+16 budget guarantees for the bracketed problem (derive analytically: bracket width / 2^16 times a bound on the residual slope over the bracket; document the derivation in a comment and in the fixture packet). Keep the tight 1e-10 check only as an early-exit fast path. Additionally handle the kink: if the bracket straddles the aperture-closure point, bisect on the kink first so each sub-interval is smooth (cheap, deterministic, keeps the secant honest).

Acceptance:
- Property test sweeping mouth pressure x bore pressure x stiffness over the supported range: zero spurious refusals, every accepted root's residual within the derived tolerance, iteration counts recorded and never exceeding the frozen budget.
- Near-kink fixtures (bracket straddling closure) converge.
- Near-miss: a genuinely bracketless/inconsistent input still refuses.
- Mutation: loosening the budget or dropping the kink-split is caught by its named fixture.
- cargo test green; wasm re-pin sweep if bytes change.
close_reason: Restored closed state after a racing claim reopened an already-completed peer fix. Original completed evidence remains authoritative: kink-first split, certified enclosure tolerance, 1800-case sweep, 9 Rust physical tests, 14 Bun physical tests, WASM 39424 bytes SHA 3b5cd291..., PHS0 validator green. No additional work or credit claimed here.

title: Measured opt-level/SIMD128 build variant decision
description:
Performance evaluation (2026-08-06 audit). The DSP crate builds at opt-level=z (size-first) with no wasm SIMD128, trading real speed in every hot loop for bytes. The piano's 72-oscillator complex-rotation loop and the guitar dual-polarization waveguide are 4x-SIMD-able. Decide with numbers, not vibes.

Evidence: dsp/concert-grand/Cargo.toml (opt-level=z, fat LTO); no `-C target-feature=+simd128` anywhere; auditor estimate ~10 flops/osc/sample piano loop (lib.rs:335-348).

Work (measurement first, per the profiling-software-performance skill discipline):
1. Build three variants: current (z), opt-level=3 no-SIMD, opt-level=3 + simd128 (simd128 needs either manual core::arch::wasm32 intrinsics in the top 2 loops or autovectorization checks — inspect the emitted wasm to confirm vector ops actually appear before crediting SIMD).
2. Measure: wasm byte size (base64-embedded delta against the root-artifact budget — PHS0 section 9 records the size liability honestly; the decoded wasm is only ~36 KB today so even 2x is small against the 7.65 MB artifact), and cold-render wall time for representative notes (low piano, guitar chord, flute) on the local engine, N>=20 renders, medians.
3. Determinism check: opt-level and SIMD reordering may change float results -> if bytes differ, that build variant requires a full re-pin sweep and re-measurement of tuning/HNR; weigh that cost in the decision.
4. Record the decision (adopt/reject/defer, with numbers) in the bead close reason and, if adopted, land the build-flag change plus re-pin sweep.

Acceptance: the three-variant measurement table exists in evidence; decision recorded; if adopted, all gates re-pinned and green. This bead may close with a reasoned "keep z" — the deliverable is the measured decision, not a mandatory flag flip.
close_reason: MEASURED DECISION: REJECT opt-level=3 and +simd128; KEEP opt-level=z. Method: three scratch builds of dsp/concert-grand replicating build-dsp.ts flags (cargo build --release --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown, RUSTFLAGS -C link-arg=--export=__heap_base; O3 via CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_OPT_LEVEL=3 env override, verified effective by size change; SIMD via -C target-feature=+simd128, verified REAL by 0xFD opcode-prefix count 412 vs 12-17 baseline noise). Direct wasm instantiation bench (bun, N=25 + N=15 confirm, medians/MAD): piano-24@96k z=50.2ms o3=60.0ms(+19% SLOWER) o3simd=66.8ms(+33% SLOWER); guitar-40@48k z=27.8 o3=25.4 o3simd=25.8; flute-72@48k z=10.2 o3=9.1 o3simd=9.3. Sizes: z=43474B(b64 57968) o3=53063B(+22%) o3simd=53800B. Output sha256 IDENTICAL across all three variants for all three cases (no re-pin would have been needed). Rationale: z wins the heaviest user-facing case (72-osc piano loop regresses badly under O3 unrolling/icache in wasm JIT; autovectorized SIMD is a further net loss), the 1-2.4ms guitar/flute gains do not justify +22% payload, and no manual-intrinsics work is warranted while the dominant case regresses. Note: bench ran on a worktree with peer chiff edits in clarinet/flute sources — all variants shared identical sources so relative comparison is valid; piano/guitar paths are untouched by that dirt. No production files changed. Harness at scratchpad/simd-eval/bench.ts.

title: Independent tuning fixture + fix measured-claim comment drift

title: Seeded per-note vibrato phase/rate/onset variation for winds
description:
Realism improvement (2026-08-06 audit, ranked cheapest-per-CPU win). Every wind note currently has IDENTICAL vibrato rate, depth, onset, and phase (phase starts at 0), so two equal notes are bit-identical and a phrase of quarter notes sounds like a sampler.

Evidence: dsp/concert-grand/src/clarinet.rs:152-155 and flute.rs:177-180 — fixed 5-ish Hz LFO, fixed depth, deterministic identical onset per note. The PHS0 gesture layer already derives a per-note deterministic seed from stable identities (sha256LowUint32 in src/audio/physical-realization.ts) and the v1 render path already receives xorshift-seeded noise — but the seed does not vary vibrato.

Fix (additive, deterministic):
1. Extend the v1 render entry points (flt_render/clr_render, and winds when they land) with an optional u32 variation seed parameter (new export names or added arg with versioned export — keep old exports byte-stable for the non-gesture path so existing pinned hashes survive where no gesture is attached).
2. In-DSP, expand the seed (xorshift step) into: vibrato initial phase (0..2pi), rate multiplier (+-4%), depth multiplier (+-10%), onset delay (+-15%). Bounds authored in the fixture packet, chosen below JND for a single note but above JND across a repeated-note pair.
3. Host: pass the existing gesture seed through renderedBufferFor into the render call, and INCLUDE the seed in the cache key only when a gesture is attached (identical notes at the same chart position repeat identically across plays — determinism law — while different events differ).
4. While the LFO code is open, replace per-sample libm::sin with a 2x2 rotation recurrence (same math the piano oscillators use) — removes a software-float sine per frame per voice. This changes bits, so it rides with this bead's re-pin rather than a separate one.

The cache key gains only the slot index, so a chart's cold renders are bounded by pitch x velocity-band x seconds-bucket x slots. title: Velocity/articulation-dependent tongued chiff attack for winds
description:
Realism improvement (2026-08-06 audit, rank 2 audible-impact-per-CPU). All wind attacks are a single first-order pressure rise (55 ms flute, 30 ms clarinet) at every velocity and register — no tongued chiff, no breath-noise transient preceding phonation. Real tongued attacks lead with a 10-30 ms noise burst and slight pressure overshoot; this is a large share of "sounds like a real flute/clarinet".

Evidence: attack envelope shaping in dsp/concert-grand/src/flute.rs and clarinet.rs (single one-pole pressure rise; auditor report section C2). The articulation gesture layer already distinguishes tongued vs legato (articulationFor in src/audio/physical-realization.ts) but the distinction is currently INAUDIBLE because curves collapse to one scalar at the v1 boundary.

Fix (additive, works with the v1 per-note path now, transfers to phrase rendering later):
1. Add a velocity- and articulation-dependent attack transient to flute/clarinet renders: shaped noise burst (band-passed turbulence, flute centered near the jet band ~1.5-3 kHz, clarinet chiff darker near 800 Hz-2 kHz) of 10-30 ms scaled by velocity, plus a brief pressure overshoot (~5-12%) with decay to the plateau operating point. Respect the operating-point plateau laws from the waveguide playbook (flute breath 0.78-0.88, clarinet 0.68-0.88): the overshoot must stay inside the speaking region or the note re-speaks late.
2. Plumb an articulation flag (tongued vs breath/legato) into the render call alongside the variation seed (same versioned-export mechanism as the vibrato-variation bead): tongued = full chiff; legato = minimal transient.
3. Keep radiated-noise band-limiting laws (playbook: ~5.5 kHz one-pole on radiated fields, direct injection <= 0.01) so HNR stays in the measured 19-37 dB band.

Acceptance:
- Measured: tongued attack has a noise-energy peak in the first 30 ms exceeding the sustain HNR floor by an authored margin; legato attack does not; time-to-peak and HNR-vs-time curves recorded in evidence.
- Tuning/HNR/brightness sustain measurements unchanged within existing bounds.
- Velocity 30 vs 110 chiff energy differs measurably and monotonically.
- Deterministic per seed; re-pin sweep; cargo + bun green. Depends on the vibrato-variation bead (shares the versioned export/seed plumbing).

title: A0/transport: refused commands leave the 'starting'/'stopping' expectation dangling
description:
Found during the studio audibility landing (jcpe-4p9s). A0 installs an
optimistic expectation via the expect-transport ephemeral intent before every
transport command (status 'starting' or 'stopping', keyed by commandRequestId).
The X1 transport publishes notifications only for receipted commands — refuse()
never publishes. So when initialize/play/pause/stop is REFUSED (engine not
ready, queue overflow, wrong state under a race), acceptTransportNotification
never fires for that request ID and the visible status sticks at
'starting'/'stopping' until the user tries again (the next expectation
overwrites it). Not a deadlock — Play stays enabled — but the status is
dishonest for its duration, and the U4 package's 'truthful audio status'
contract cannot be satisfied while the gap exists.

The A0 EphemeralIntent union has no way to settle or roll back an installed
expectation (statuses are only 'starting'|'stopping'; acceptTransportNotification
requires a genuine notification; fabricating one would be dishonest). Fix needs
an A0-contract-level settlement path, e.g. a 'settle-transport-expectation'
intent carrying the refusal outcome (commandRequestId + refusal code + the
transport's actual state echoed from TransportCommandRefusal.state), plus the
edit-plan/state-contract fixture re-pin that entails, plus controller wiring in
playProgression/pauseProgression/stopProgression where the async outcomes are
currently discarded (void). Belongs naturally with the U4 build
(jcpe-milestone-reliable-studio-l3a.12.2) or immediately before it.
close_reason: Fixed in 51b1240. A0 contract section 13 (additive): 13th ephemeral intent settle-transport-expectation carrying the refused commandRequestId, dispatch-time documentId/planRevision, the transport's echoed state projected to a settled status (locked/disposed→unavailable), and failureCode (engineRefusalCode ?? code). Accepts only over a still-optimistic matching slot, else ignored-stale — a genuine notification always wins; malformed refuses transport.expectation_invalid. Controller settleRefusedTransport wired in playProgression (initialize+play outcomes), pauseProgression, stopProgression. Packet: A0-UI-012/013/014, TR-A0-TRANSPORT-SETTLE, A0-MUT-031/032; counts 68 state cases/35 gaps/32 controls/54 links/42 linked/19 traces/21 owners re-pinned across manifest, validate-a0-contract.ts, verify-a0-evidence.ts, three conformance tests. Proof: tests/unit/studio-transport-refusal.test.ts drives REAL X1 refusals (pause-before-init settles stopping→unavailable+transport.locked; play-while-playing settles starting→playing+transport.state_invalid; next expectation clears the cause; replay/late/old-request all ignored-stale). bun test 2790/0, Playwright 483/0 ×3 engines, validate:a0-contract pass, live-verified on jazzchords.org (artifact c04e2ade).

title: Engine: one render refusal poisons the session (fault cascade until reload)
description:
Split from jcpe-live-audio-error-61c5e018-609d (P0 evidence bead) so this engine bug cannot be lost inside the artifact post-mortem: ROOT CAUSE 2 of the 2026-08-07 live breakage — REFUSAL->FAULT CASCADE. The engine never recovers.

Repro driver: scratchpad/repro-61c5/drive*.mjs (session-scoped; re-derive from the bead evidence if expired). Fix in src/audio/audio-engine.ts (+controller if the fault latch lives there); regression fixture: refuse-then-switch-then-play must succeed (the RC2 recovery fixture proposed in the parent bead's playback-gate design).

Also note the sibling design decision recorded on the parent bead: hard model pitch windows vs voice-assignment register shifting (product call, rebuild-owner territory) — this bead is ONLY the recovery bug.

title: U1 spec packet: four quick-entry corpus cases disagree with the T0 grammar they assume
notes:
Found by the U1 verify leaf (jcpe-milestone-reliable-studio-l3a.10.3) while replaying the byte-pinned corpus `tests/fixtures/editing/quick-entry-cases.json` against the real controller. The corpus sets `t0ResultIsScenarioInput: true`, so each case's `t0Result` is an assumption; these four cases assume a parse the real T0 grammar does not produce, which leaves their declared U1 classification describing a parse that never happens.

1. U1-QE-046 transposes the annotation and the duration. The case writes `| Cmaj7 "head in":4 |` and expects a parsed draft. The T0 grammar carries an event annotation after the duration: `| Cmaj7:4 "head in" |` parses with annotation="head in", while the case's own text is refused as chart.unsupported_notation. The case note ("an event annotation is inert data carried through unchanged") states the right intent; only the draft text is wrong.

2. U1-QE-030 contradicts U1-QE-013. It assumes `| C:4 | | ` is refused with chart.unsupported_notation; U1-QE-013 states that two adjacent boundary tokens deliberately enclose one empty measure, and T0 accepts the draft.

3. U1-QE-033 contradicts U1-QE-006. It assumes `| C |` is refused with chart.layout_invalid; U1-QE-006 states that T0 allocates the whole bar to the single undurated slot, and T0 accepts the draft.

4. U1-QE-026, U1-QE-027 and U1-QE-036 under-state T0's recovery set: T0 recovers one chord after a forbidden fragment header, two chords from `| C:4 | D`, and every chord of the overfilled bar, where the cases assume none, one and none.

Separately, `tokenStates` is authored per case with no stated total projection, and two pairs cannot be reconciled by any single rule over the declared T0 result: U1-QE-021 (two recovered chords, one non-fill diagnostic, no invalid row) against U1-QE-030 (one recovered chord, one non-fill diagnostic, one invalid row); and U1-QE-036 (one invalid row for four hundred unrecovered chords) against U1-QE-025 (one invalid row for one). The verify leaf asserts only the projection law U1 owns and leaves the invalid-row rule to the packet.

Nothing here changes production behaviour: the U1 classification laws hold against the real parse in every case, and the conformance replay asserts them. What is needed is a packet decision — re-pin the affected cases against the real grammar, or state why the assumed outcomes are correct and T0 must change. The divergences are named in T0_SCENARIO_DIVERGENCES in tests/conformance/u1-production-conformance.test.ts so a fifth one cannot appear unnoticed.
close_reason:
Resolved as a packet correction: the corpus was wrong, T0 was right, and the divergence list is now empty.

## How each answer was derived

Not from the parser. Every replacement value comes from `docs/T0_SYNTAX_CONTRACT.md` plus the independently authored T0 packet `tests/fixtures/theory/chart-cases.json`, which pins the same shapes:

- `T0-CHART-ERR-007` (`@meter 4/4\nC`) declares `insertableCount: 1` — the fragment header refuses the draft and T0 still publishes the chord after the LF.
- `T0-CHART-ERR-013` (`| C:4`) declares `insertableCount: 1` for an unclosed measure.
- `T0-CHART-ERR-019` (`| C:3 Dm:2 |`) declares `insertableDurations: ["explicit:3/1", "explicit:2/1"]` — **every** chord of an overfilled bar is recovered, not none.
- `T0-CHART-ERR-031` (`C | D:4 |`) declares the mixed pair literally: the undurated chord as `duration.kind: requires-caller` with reason `chart.layout_invalid`, the durated one as resolved.
- Contract 5.2 orders the event as `chord-symbol duration? (hspace json-string)?` and states that two adjacent boundary tokens enclose an empty measure; 5.7 step 5 divides the whole bar among undurated slots; 5.8 resumes recovery after an explicit LF.

## The six cases

| Case | What was wrong | Correction |
|---|---|---|
| U1-QE-026 | declared no recovery after `chart.header_forbidden_in_fragment` | publishes `C` (resolved 4/1), per 5.8 and T0-CHART-ERR-007 |
| U1-QE-027 | declared one recovered chord for `\| C:4 \| D` | publishes both: `C` resolved, `D` requires-caller |
| U1-QE-030 | declared `\| C:4 \| \| ` refused, contradicting its own sibling U1-QE-013 | restated as the positive it is — a barred sequence whose last measure is empty parses, and the empty final measure is carried into the section rather than dropped or joined. Draft text untouched. |
| U1-QE-033 | the draft `\| C \|` cannot produce the `requires-caller` recovery the case is *for*: 5.7 allocates the whole bar, exactly as U1-QE-006 states | draft corrected to `C \| D:4 \|`, the shape T0-CHART-ERR-031 pins. The case keeps its declared expectation, its kind, and its law links. |
| U1-QE-036 | declared no recovery from the overfilled bar | publishes all 1,024 chords, per T0-CHART-ERR-019; `canInsertOneChord` becomes true because one recovered chord fits the empty destination |
| U1-QE-046 | the draft wrote the annotation before the duration | draft corrected to `\| Cmaj7:4 "head in" \|`; the case's own note already stated the right intent |

Only two drafts changed, and in both the draft is what contradicted the published grammar. Four cases kept their pinned input and had their declared T0 result corrected.

## The unstated projection, now stated and enforced

The separate half of this bug was that `tokenStates` was authored per case with no total rule, so two pairs could not be reconciled. The rule production actually holds is one line of `StudioQuickEntryToken`'s own contract: a refused draft yields one `insertable` row per recovered chord **plus one `invalid` row per T0 diagnostic**. Under it, eight further cases were short a row — U1-QE-021, 023, 024, 031, 032, 034 and 035 alongside the six above — and none of those eight had been noticed, because the replay was only counting insertable rows.

- The corpus now states it in `classificationPolicy.tokenStateProjection` (parsed / refused / unparsed / truncation).
- `scripts/validate-u1-contract.ts` recomputes the whole ordered sequence per case and compares element by element, and separately requires the projection statement to be present and unrestated. Counting insertable rows alone let a case drop its diagnostic rows silently; that hole is closed.

title: OWNER: which license grant applies to vendored FrankenSim files?
description:
Owner decision required before any FrankenSim file is vendored into this repository (foundry or runtime).

Question: For Rust files vendored from /dp/frankensim (surveyed at commit b47259187a31b704f8f0faf6abdf49b32919b96a) into this repository's offline foundry — and potentially fs-math into the runtime WASM crate — which license grant applies: (a) the frankensim repository-level MIT License with OpenAI/Anthropic Rider, or (b) the per-crate "MIT OR Apache-2.0" declared in /dp/frankensim/Cargo.toml [workspace.package]? And what provenance text must each vendored file carry?

(d) CONTEXTUAL RESOLUTION — deterministic key inference over the weighted pitch-class stream (frozen profile table, total tie-break); re-rank resolveSonority alternatives by inferred key and neighbor context (reuse H0 analyzeChartEvent machinery via interface injection; theory stays pure, never imports the Atlas); spelling follows the inferred key instead of the fixed canonical table. Transposition equivariance is a law: transposing all input notes by k semitones transposes the inferred key and every emitted symbol identically.
(e) FORM — SMF marker events (already decoded into tracks[].markers) become named sections splitting the import; files without markers import as one section named from the file name (current law retained). Pickup/anacrusis: notes before the first full bar form a pickup measure under the existing MeasureCompletion pickup law, never silently dropped.
(f) SETTINGS TRANSFER — commit applies the file's initial tempo (per makeTempoBpm law); when the destination chart is empty/starter, also the file's meter, the inferred key, and the document title (from file/track name); an occupied chart's meter/key/title are NEVER silently rewritten — the card states what was and wasn't applied and why. Mid-file tempo/meter changes beyond the first are reported in the result card and trace, never silently ignored.
(g) GROOVE MATCH — deterministic feature extraction (swing ratio from off-beat onset placement, tempo band, onset density, bar-cycle evenness) mapped to the six reviewed groove ids by a stated total scoring function with declared tie-break order; scope is SELECTION-ONLY per jcpe-61zo default (creation lanes B/C documented as extension points, not implemented); the choice must carry human-readable evidence sentences ("Medium swing: swing ratio 1.9:1 at 132 BPM") — chosen, stated, and overridable, never hidden.
(h) AUTOMATION ENVELOPE — the whole gesture (insert + tempo + meter + key + title + groove) lands as one comprehensible undo unit or a stated, counted sequence the result card announces; the >4096-code-point route is specified (chunked insert-fragment sequence with stated undo story, and/or replace-document origin canonical-import when the destination is the starter chart) rather than a dead end.
(i) IMPORTTRACE — a frozen machine-readable diagnostics schema attached to every preview: per-stage records (decode, salvage, classification, segmentation, key inference, resolution, groove match, plan) with input hashes, counts, every decision and its reason, and deterministic work counters. This is the logging backbone the M1 unit and e2e tests assert against and dump on failure.
(j) DETERMINISM — identical bytes produce identical previews, traces, and plans; every bounded search states its work/state/memory bounds; wall time is never a musical cutoff.

FIXTURE DISCIPLINE: every law above gets positive, negative/near-miss, transposition, and mutation-control fixtures, independently authored (never derived from production output), including at least one multi-track fixture with drums+bass+comping+melody, one arpeggiated/rubato fixture, one marker-form fixture, one pickup fixture, one mid-file tempo-change fixture, and per-groove-id feel fixtures for the matcher.

title: iOS: Cadd9 parses as a dominant ninth (dead add9 branch)
description:
Background (audit 2026-09-01 @ 2909fe8): ios/Sources/JazzTheory.swift chord-quality resolution checks lower.contains("9") (line ~168) BEFORE the lower == "add9" branch (line ~177), so the add9 branch is dead code and Cadd9 parses as a dominant ninth [0,4,7,10,14] — WITH a flat seventh. The bundled library entry that uses it (ios/Sources/JazzLibrary.swift line ~26, entry annotated "Add-nine major colors without the seventh") therefore plays four chords that directly contradict the entry's own description. add2 is unaffected (reaches its branch). This is a literal-facts violation — the product family's core promise is that the literal chord row never lies.

Approach: reorder/specialize the suffix matching so add9 (and any addN) resolves before the generic contains("9") dominant path; audit the whole resolution ladder for other order-dependent dead branches (the same pattern class produced the alt/#11 dropping tracked in the extensions bead). Add unit tests: Cadd9 -> [0,4,7,14] (no 10), Cadd2, C9 unchanged, and a library-integrity test asserting the glass-lab/add-nine entries' parsed tones contain no minor seventh. Keep the parser bounded and total (refusal, never guess).

Acceptance: Cadd9 tones correct in inspector, audio, and MIDI export; new tests green in FrankenJazzTests; no existing test regressed. Test plan: parser unit tests + one store-level test loading the affected library entry and asserting rendered pitch classes. Non-goals: extending grammar coverage (separate extensions bead); web-side T0 (unaffected — verified separately).
acceptance_criteria: Cadd9 tones correct in inspector/audio/MIDI; parser-order audit done; library-integrity test green
