title: iOS: explicit-duration formatting breaks round-trip; app refuses its own chart text
description:
Background (audit 2026-09-01 @ 2909fe8): the explicit beat-duration feature (commit e371cd9) formats durations by truncating to 3 decimals (ios/Sources/JazzTheory.swift formatBeatDuration, ~lines 119-122). Round-trip failure: enter "| C:2 D E F |" (4/4) -> remainder distributes as 2/3-beat notes -> formatter emits "| C:2 D:0.667 E:0.667 F:0.667 |" -> re-parse sums to 4.001 beats -> .invalidMeasureDuration refusal (line ~87). The store then writes the refused text back into draftText (JazzStudioStore.swift ~324/362), leaving the editor showing permanently-invalid text, and the .chartText EXPORT writes a file FrankenJazz itself cannot re-import. The existing test (testQuickEntryDistributesUnspecifiedRemainderAndRefusesOverfill) uses a remainder that divides evenly and so never hits the bug.

Approach: make format/parse a closed round trip. Options: (1) formatter emits exact rational text (e.g. fractions "2/3" — the web app's exact-rational-time doctrine, preferred for parity with jcpe-cu6k's exact-duration entry work); (2) parser accepts a bounded epsilon when explicit durations were formatter-produced — weaker, rejected unless (1) is infeasible in scope. Whichever is chosen, the invariant to test is: for every chart the app can hold, format(parse(format(x))) == format(x) and parse(format(x)) succeeds. Also stop persisting refused text into draftText: a failed re-parse of the app's own formatting must surface as a bug, not as user-visible invalid state.

Acceptance: property-style round-trip test over generated charts including thirds/sixths/sevenths remainders; the "| C:2 D E F |" case specifically; chart-text export/import round-trip test; no refused-text-in-draft state reachable from formatter output. Non-goals: changing the duration grammar the user types; web-side E0 formats.
acceptance_criteria: format/parse closed round trip incl. thirds remainders; refused-own-output state unreachable; export/import round-trip test green

title: iOS: slash-chord bass parsed and displayed but never sounded or exported
description:
Background (audit 2026-09-01 @ 2909fe8): ios/Sources/JazzTheory.swift parses slash-chord bass (ChordDescription.bass, ~lines 145-150, 205) and the UI displays it, but bass is read NOWHERE in voicing(), the additive renderer, or MIDIFileWriter — so Cm/B and Cm/Bb sound identical with C in the bass, in audio AND in exported MIDI. The bundled "lament" library entry (JazzLibrary.swift ~line 18) is described as "One bass line walks down a fourth"; the stated musical point of that entry does not exist in sound. This is a manual-means-exact violation: the symbol says the bass, the sound ignores it.

Approach: thread bass through voicing (lowest voice = spelled bass pitch class, register-placed below the chord body; refuse only where range makes it impossible and say so), through the renderer's pitch set, and through MIDI export note events. Verify against the plan's voicing-family expectations (rootless families must still honor an explicit slash bass — the bass is a literal fact, not a family suggestion). Add tests: parse/voice/export for Cm/Bb asserting the exported MIDI's lowest note is Bb; a library-integrity test that the lament entry's four bass notes descend as annotated; renderer smoke asserting the bass frequency present.

Acceptance: slash bass audible and exported; lament entry demonstrably walks; tests green. Non-goals: contextual bass-line generation; web app (its V0/V1 engines already honor slash bass per contract).

title: iOS: function labels wrong in ordinary cases (E7-in-C Tonic, maj7 Dominant pull)
description:
Background (audit 2026-09-01 @ 2909fe8): ios/Sources/JazzTheory.swift function labeling (~lines 187-191) misreads ordinary jazz cases: (1) [0,4,9].contains(relative) labels ANY chord on scale degrees 1/3/6 "Tonic family", so E7 in C — a secondary dominant V/vi, and the opening chord of the bundled ragtime entry — is labeled Tonic. (2) The fallback `|| lower.contains("7")` labels any symbol containing the character "7" as "Dominant pull", so Ebmaj7 and Abmaj7 in C read as dominants (the glass-lab entry collects three such labels in four bars). The app's own plan promises literal/contextual separation with honest uncertainty; these labels are confidently wrong in cases the bundled library itself exercises.

Approach: minimum honest fix — quality-aware roles: dominant function requires dominant-quality structure (major third + minor seventh) or explicit leading-tone resolution context; major-seventh chords never read "Dominant pull"; chords outside the diatonic set get an honest "chromatic/borrowed — no functional claim" rather than a forced family. Follow the web app's precedent (src/theory/chart-analysis.ts states its own scope limits in its header; the shipped Harmony Lens says "No key is set, so no functional reading is claimed"). Where confidence is low, SAY less. Sweep all 25 library entries and assert no label contradicts the entry's own annotation.

Acceptance: E7-in-C no longer "Tonic family"; no maj7 chord labeled dominant; library sweep test green; labels for out-of-key chords are explicitly non-committal. Test plan: table-driven unit tests over (key, symbol) -> label including the ragtime and glass-lab cases. Non-goals: porting the full web H0 evidence-tier engine; Roman-numeral rendering changes beyond what the label fix forces.
acceptance_criteria: Quality-aware labels; no maj7 reads dominant; out-of-key chords non-committal; full library sweep green

title: iOS: extensions silently dropped (#11/alt) and pitch classes flattened mod 12
description:
Background (audit 2026-09-01 @ 2909fe8): two related literal-facts defects in ios/Sources/JazzTheory.swift. (1) Extensions silently dropped: Fmaj7#11 matches the maj7 branch (~line 164) -> [0,4,7,11]; the #11 vanishes from tones, voicing, audio, and MIDI — while the lush-ballad-study library entry uses exactly that symbol. A7alt -> plain [0,4,7,10] while colorNote (~line 197) still announces "Altered dominant tension": the inspector's Literal row and its color note contradict each other. (2) Upstream cause for voicing crudeness: ChordDescription.pitchClasses is stored mod 12 (~line 207), destroying above-octave placement (a 13th's 14 and 21 arrive as 2 and 9) before voicing runs, producing five-note clusters inside one octave.

Approach: either implement the extension (parse #11/b9/#9/b13/alt tensions into real tone sets and preserve octave placement into voicing) or refuse honestly (unknown-suffix refusal with the diagnostic naming the unsupported fragment — the family rule is never silently guess). Given the library uses these symbols, implementing at least #11/9/13/alt-partial is the likely right scope; align colorNote text with what the tone set actually contains so the two rows can never disagree (derive the note from the parsed tensions, not the raw string). Fix pitchClasses to preserve interval structure above the octave for voicing input.

Acceptance: for every symbol in JazzLibrary.swift, inspector Literal row == sounded tones == exported MIDI tones, and colorNote claims only what the tone set contains; unsupported syntax refuses with a named fragment; voicing no longer collapses extensions into one octave. Test plan: per-symbol table test over the full library; A7alt and Fmaj7#11 specifically; a refusal case. Non-goals: full T0-grammar parity with the web parser (track separately if desired); changing the five family algorithms (D6 owns spread).
acceptance_criteria: Literal row == sounded == exported for every library symbol; unsupported syntax refuses with named fragment
notes: Fully addressed by published commit 847b783. Exact closed suffix grammar now implements maj7#11, 7alt, b5/#5/b9/#9, 6/9, and 9/11/13 with octave-aware intervals; unsupported suffixes refuse with the named fragment; voicing/audio/MIDI export use the same literal sounded tones. Evidence: docs/evidence/IOS_EXTENSION_TRUTH_2026-09-01.md. Gates: focused Catalyst 3/3, full Catalyst 38/38, generic iOS build green, UBS reviewed, git diff --check clean.
close_reason: Extension truth, octave-aware voicing, named unsupported-suffix refusal, library-wide literal/sounded/export consistency, and recorded evidence are complete.

title: iOS: promised gaps - spread voicing, transition motion, Reduce Motion, Save Copy, Catalyst Dynamic Type

title: iOS release readiness: entitlements, icon asset hygiene, regenerate-and-diff project gate
description:
Background (audit 2026-09-01 @ 2909fe8): App Store submission blockers and hygiene in ios/: (1) No .entitlements file exists anywhere (find for *.entitlements returns nothing) — a Mac Catalyst App Store build requires App Sandbox entitlements; document-based file access needs the right user-selected-file entitlements. (2) Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset contains an orphaned FrankenJazz-AppIcon-1024.png (RGBA) not referenced by Contents.json (the referenced icon is the correct opaque RGB 1024 from 99decab) — Xcode warns, and the stray file invites re-regression of the alpha-channel validation failure that 99decab fixed. (3) MonsterIcon.imageset declares 1x/2x/3x but supplies only 1x (two unassigned slots) and uses a 1024pt image in a ~48-62pt frame. (4) MARKETING_VERSION 0.1.0 / CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION 1 — fine for now, but version/build bump policy is undocumented. (5) ios/README.md:50 says the xcodeproj is generated by XcodeGen, yet FrankenJazz.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj is committed — acceptable, but then the "clean generated-project rebuild" acceptance gate can silently pass on a stale committed file; make the gate regenerate and diff.

Approach: add App Sandbox entitlements (read/write user-selected files; no network — consistent with PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy's no-tracking declaration and the offline product boundary); delete or wire the orphaned icon; fix MonsterIcon slots/size; write the version-bump note into ios/README.md; make the regenerate-and-diff check part of the evidence bead's script.

Acceptance: xcodegen-regenerated project diffs clean against committed; asset catalogs produce zero Xcode warnings; entitlements present and consistent with the privacy manifest; archive validation passes (recorded in the evidence bead). Non-goals: actual App Store submission; signing-team changes.
acceptance_criteria: Entitlements present and privacy-consistent; zero asset warnings; regenerated project diffs clean
notes: Release-readiness hygiene completed. Removed the tracked unreferenced RGBA AppIcon duplicate; replaced the 1024px 1x MonsterIcon plus empty slots with deterministic 64/128/192px approved-artwork variants; documented generated-project diff and version/build bump laws. Verified xcodegen regeneration diff is clean, generic iOS Simulator build exit 0 with zero asset warnings, Catalyst 38/38, Catalyst entitlement path/bundle settings, sandbox + user-selected read/write with no network entitlement, zero-tracking/zero-collection privacy manifest, opaque 1024 app icon, and unsigned generic-iOS archive exit 0. Evidence: docs/evidence/IOS_RELEASE_READINESS_2026-09-01.md. Apple remote signing/notarization/App Store validation not claimed.

title: iOS: recorded test-run evidence protocol plus recovery/voicing test holes
description:
Background (audit 2026-09-01 @ 2909fe8): ios/ has real tests — Tests/FrankenJazzCoreTests.swift (18 tests: parser beats/refusals, all-25-library-entries pitch-range compile, transposition, MIDI header/length, export->import round trip, hostile MIDI matrix, determinism, store-level import) and UITests/FrankenJazzUITests.swift (3 tests: playback, library load, document sheet) — but ZERO evidence any of it has ever run: no CI config anywhere in the repo (no .github/), no .xctestplan, no xcresult, no recorded simulator output, and release-evidence/ contains only web-audio artifacts. Every acceptance gate in docs/APPLE_APP_PLAN.md (iPhone sim matrix incl. relaunch-recovery and Dynamic Type screenshots; iPad split layouts; Catalyst build/resize/menus/file-open; unit-test gate; clean generated-project rebuild) is therefore unproven. Known test holes: JazzRecoveryStore is private with NO recovery round-trip test (a plan-named gate), and voicing coverage is only "pitches in range". Also recovery I/O is synchronous on the main actor on every mutation (JazzStudioStore.swift ~364) — plausible hitch on 512-measure charts; measure it while the harness exists.

Approach: this machine is Linux — the deliverable is the *recorded evidence protocol plus its first executed run on a Mac*, mirroring the web side's hash-bound ledger discipline: a script (xcodebuild test with -resultBundlePath) that emits an xcresult summary JSON checked into release-evidence/ios/ with commit hash, Xcode/simulator versions, and pass counts; the APPLE_APP_PLAN gate checklist executed once with screenshots attached; new tests closing the recovery round-trip and voicing holes (writable from any platform now, runnable on the Mac). If the owner wants CI, GitHub Actions macos runner is the obvious shape, but a manually-executed recorded protocol satisfies the plan's gates — agent-authored results must not masquerade as the human review the plan requires (fresh-eyes review row stays human).

Acceptance: release-evidence/ios/ contains a hash-bound run record showing all unit+UI tests green at a named commit; recovery round-trip and voicing tests exist and are included; the plan's gate checklist has a recorded first pass (or honest per-row failures spawning follow-up beads). Non-goals: web e2e; App Store submission.
acceptance_criteria: release-evidence/ios/ hash-bound run record all-green at named commit; recovery round-trip and voicing tests exist
notes: Published source commit be16246 adds isolated recovery dependency injection plus tests for valid round-trip, corrupt-current fallback to the previous validated copy, and real JazzStudioStore startup recovery. It also proves all six voicing families deterministic, distinct, ordered, unique, bounded, and slash-bass-correct. Recorded local Mac evidence is release-evidence/ios/be16246-local-xcode.json: Catalyst units 42/42, iPhone 17 Pro iOS 26.1 UI 6/6, generic iOS Simulator build PASS, XcodeGen drift gate PASS, all bound to published commit be16246 and source hashes. title: iOS MIDI import: salvage ordinary DAW quirks instead of refusing (verify post-2909fe8 first)
description:
Background (audit 2026-09-01 @ 2909fe8, partially addressed by 2909fe8 "tolerate conventional metadata safely" — RE-VERIFY FIRST): ios/Sources/MIDIFileImporter.swift is far stricter than its own docstring ("ordinary SMF 0/1"): at audit time it threw on any re-struck note before release (~line 606), any unmatched note-off (~611), any unterminated note (~638), missing/misplaced end-of-track (~637), any non-4/4 meter anywhere (~160-165), and meta payloads over 1KB (~538). Real DAW exports routinely produce the first three (overlapping takes, sustain-pedal artifacts). The UI copy (FrankenJazzStudioView.swift ~858) warns only about meter and unnameable harmony, so other refusals feel arbitrary. FrankenJazz's own exports round-trip cleanly, which is why the test suite doesn't catch it. Note 2909fe8 already relaxed some metadata handling — diff current behavior against this list before working.

Approach: for each strictness, decide salvage-vs-refuse using the web app's M0 doctrine as precedent (V2R-13 "never refuse a whole file for content-level defects"; salvage ledger reporting what was repaired/dropped): re-struck note -> treat as retrigger (implicit note-off), unmatched note-off -> ignore with ledger entry, unterminated note -> close at track end with ledger entry, missing EOT -> synthesize at last event. Keep hard refusals for structural corruption (bad VLQ, truncation, SMPTE, format 2) and keep every resource ceiling. Surface the salvage ledger in the import UI the way the web preview does, and align the warning copy with the real refusal set.

Acceptance: a corpus of representative DAW-exported files (Logic/GarageBand/Reaper patterns with overlaps and pedal CCs) imports with honest salvage notes instead of refusing; hostile-MIDI tests still refuse; UI copy matches behavior. Test plan: extend the hostile/tolerance test matrix with the overlap/unmatched/unterminated cases both ways. Non-goals: format-2 support; tempo-map import beyond current scope.
acceptance_criteria: DAW-pattern corpus imports with salvage ledger; hostile cases still refuse; UI copy matches behavior
notes: Implemented and locally verified in published source commits 0396c5c and e64df0c. Conventional DAW retriggers, stray note-offs, track-end-open notes, and missing EOT markers now salvage with an explicit four-counter user-visible ledger; structural corruption, resource ceilings, unsupported meter, format 2, SMPTE, and unnameable harmony still refuse. Evidence: docs/evidence/IOS_MIDI_SALVAGE_2026-09-02.md. Gates: focused Catalyst 4/4, full Catalyst 40/40, generic iOS Simulator build green, focused iPhone UI 1/1 after an honestly recorded runner loss and query-ceiling test correction, git diff --check clean. UBS findings reviewed: 41 criticals are false positives on SwiftUI Font.system calls; no shell/process execution.
close_reason: DAW-pattern salvage, explicit repair ledger, hostile structural refusals, aligned UI copy, and recorded local proof are complete.

title: Instrument selection requires manual refresh: newly selected physical instruments do not take effect live
description: Owner report (2026-08-08, live studio): many of the new instruments cannot be dynamically selected — the selection does not take effect until a manual browser refresh. Older oscillator instruments switch live correctly. Reproduce across a physical (WASM/waveguide) instrument and a legacy oscillator instrument: select while idle and while playing; expected: the next attack uses the newly selected instrument without a page reload; actual (owner): refresh required. Investigate the setInstrument -> rideLiveInstrument -> audio prepare/recipe path and the boot-time renderer initialization for selection-time gaps. Distinct from the timbre-quality campaigns (jcpe-plucked-quality-body-amp-6yg6 closed 2026-08-08, jcpe-winds-quality-triangulation-drga in flight): this bug is about selection plumbing, not sound character.

comments.author: SwiftBridge
comments.text:
2026-08-08 SwiftBridge root-cause + state record.

REPRODUCTION (real browser, deployed-equivalent bytes = tracked HEAD artifact = live site):
- tests/e2e/j4hj-repro.spec.ts (untracked): idle selection of all 15 instruments reaches data-audio-state=playing on Chromium AND WebKit. Selection plumbing is sound while idle.
- tests/e2e/j4hj-midrun.spec.ts (untracked): mid-run physical-instrument swaps on the HEAD artifact: after 1-2 successful cycles the engine faults (data-audio-state=failed), and EVERY subsequent Play refuses with 'The browser needs a fresh click before audio can start' forever — only a page reload recovers. Timing-dependent trigger, 100% consistent cascade once triggered.

ROOT CAUSE (two parts):
1. Trigger: engine faults after a few play/stop/swap cycles with physical instruments at HEAD (wasm renderer path; the physics campaign's uncommitted edits touch exactly this area).
2. Unrecoverability: deployed src/ui/App.tsx hardcodes sequence: 1 in three gesture callsites, but the X1 transport requires a strictly increasing gesture sequence after the first accepted gesture (transport.gesture_invalid / audio.gesture_sequence_invalid). After any fault, fault --initialize-transport (trusted gesture)--> ready is unreachable because the app can never mint sequence > 1. Page reload resets the transport counter, hence 'refresh fixes it'.

STATE OF FIX:
- The unrecoverability is FIXED in the current worktree by the physics campaign (App.tsx nextAudioGesture stride allocation, STUDIO_AUDIO_GESTURE_SEQUENCE_STRIDE = 21, exported via src/application/runtime.ts; studio-audio resume retries increment within the reserved stride). NOT committed, NOT deployed.
- Independent verification on the dev server (campaign tree): all 10 mid-run physical swap cycles survive (run stays playing).
- The deployed artifact still carries the bug until the campaign's work lands and deploys.

Findings shared with PearlChapel (campaign coordinator) via agent mail thread jcpe-j4hj-refresh-bug. Repro specs offered for the campaign's evidence pack. Environment note: the omp browser-tool Chromium has an AudioContext sampleRate quirk (reports 48000, true rate 44100 -> audio.graph_create_failed via ConvolverNode rate check); project Playwright Chromium is truthful (verified).

title: Hybrid sampled-piano attack layer over the synth sustain (owner-approved tone direction)
description: Owner 2026-07-29 after listening: synthesis alone still sounds nothing like a warm Steinway in a hall; approved HYBRID (~3-4 MB): real recorded attack transients layered over the existing Rust/WASM synth sustain+decay. Plan: (1) source a CC0/CC-BY sampled grand (e.g. Salamander Grand CC-BY, or University of Iowa MIS public-domain piano) - record provenance+license in the build inventory as a THIRD embedded asset; (2) pick ~8-12 pitches x 2-3 velocity layers, first ~300-400ms only (attack+early body), resampled to 32-44.1kHz mono/stereo, encoded (Opus/AAC in a data: URI decoded via decodeAudioData - NOTE that needs an AudioContextPort method + X0 amendment, OR raw PCM in the wasm memory to avoid new browser API surface); (3) cross-fade sample attack into the wasm-rendered sustain at ~250-350ms with per-note gain matching so the seam is inaudible (measure: spectral continuity + no level step >1dB at the splice); (4) pitch-shift between sampled keys by resampling within +/-3 semitones. Gates: THD<0.6% preserved, spectral centroid/decay metrics, audible 3/3, and OWNER LISTENING as the final gate. Requires the size-ceiling raise bead first.
notes: MIX + PERF ROUND (2026-07-29): crossfade was destructively cancelling (109/440 note-velocity pairs >=3dB, worst -14.4dB) - fixed via coherence measurement + polarity correction + compensated weights (10/440, worst -4.0dB). Key pan narrowed twice (+/-0.75 -> 0.22 -> 0.10) after rendered stems showed the mix leaning 4.4dB left / bass stem 8dB. RENDER COST was starving Firefox's main thread (2 scheduler ticks/run, silent playback): fixed by (a) wasm honouring a requested length instead of always synthesizing the full decay, (b) one buffer per velocity BAND not per shade, (c) MAX_PARTIALS 48->24. Firefox now 91 ticks, peak 0.41.
close_reason: Hybrid sampled attack shipped+deployed. 66 slices (22 pitches x 3 velocity buckets, 400ms, 44.1kHz 16-bit mono, 2,328,480 raw bytes) covering all 88 keys; equal-power crossfade 180-320ms into the unchanged wasm sustain. Measured corrections: per-slice microphone selection (mono-summing phase-cancelled the transient), per-slice stretch-tuning cents (1.32c mean disagreement from 5.57), slew-limited duck replacing a scalar limiter that tore a 6dB hole at the seam. Centroid roughly doubles in the bottom four octaves; top two darken. THD worst 0.5634% (gate 0.6%), peak 0.95, seam step 0.0874 (gate 0.15). Salamander Grand Piano V3 CC-BY-3.0 credited in-artifact + license inventory (3 assets). Gates: 11 new hybrid tests, suite 2626/0, audible 3/3, build/licenses green, artifact 4,180,328 B of 8,388,608. FINAL GATE REMAINS OWNER LISTENING.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ROOT-CAUSE EVIDENCE (read-only forensics on shipped artifact 61c5e018; full matrices + PCM captures in scratchpad/repro-61c5/).

ARTIFACT SELF-CONSISTENCY: REFUTED as cause — embedded wasm sha 572f51b9... matches the committed embed exactly (106,682 bytes) and exports every expected symbol (plk_note_frames/plk_render, flt_/clr_ expressive set).

RC1 — PLUCKED RANGE REFUSALS (the owner's "audio error" on new instruments): plucked.rs midi_range: guitars/dreadnought (40,88), ukulele (60,93), upright (28,62). The shared immutable chart plan sends chord-voicing pitches outside those windows (ukulele: most voicing notes sit below C4=60; upright: chord tones above 62; guitars: notes below 40/above 88). plk_note_frames returns 0 out-of-range -> renderNote null -> whole-command refusal -> status "The audio engine refused the command. Press Stop, then Play." ISOLATED per-instrument browser matrix (fresh page each): ALL FIVE plucked models refuse mid-chart (3-12 buffers rendered, then refusal); all legacy instruments play clean in isolation. Offline gates missed it because every plucked test swept single notes INSIDE each model's range; nothing played an actual chart.

RC2 — REFUSAL->FAULT CASCADE (why the owner saw "audio error" on EVERYTHING): sequential browser run (one page, switching instruments): after guitar's refusal, every subsequent instrument INCLUDING legacy sampled models reports "Audio hit a fault. Press Play to restart it." (upright-bass sampled, concert-vibes, clarinet all faulted sequentially yet play clean in isolation). The engine does not recover across instrument switch + Play after a mid-chart refusal. Engine state-machine bug, distinct from RC1; needs its own regression test in the rebuild (refuse mid-chart, switch instrument, Play must succeed).

RC3 — FLUTE OUT-OF-REGISTER DEGRADATION (the owner's "flute sounds super fucked up"): the chart sends the flute voicing notes down to MIDI 45-53. A/B PCM capture (same chart position, old 67b9ae08 vs shipped 61c5e018): OLD renders MIDI 47-48 voices at ~131-132 Hz, HNR 34-40 dB; NEW renders the same voices at 128.6-130.5 Hz (up to -29 cents) with HNR down to 7.5 dB (breath-noise-dominated). The winds reference gate only measured in-register cells (C4+), while production playback exercises the low extension. Rebuild must either register-shift per-instrument voicing assignment (product decision) or gate the FULL pitch range any chart can send.

PROPOSAL (Phase-4, NOT implemented per coordinator scope): predeploy:playback — a real-browser per-instrument playback gate run against the BUILT artifact before any deploy: serve artifact on loopback; for EVERY instrument option: fresh page, select, Play >=4 s, assert (a) status stays "Playing" (no refusal/fault strings), (b) >=N audible rendered buffers via an AudioContext.createBuffer tap (init-script, no app changes), (c) per-buffer pitch sanity: every rendered f0 within tolerance of SOME chart pitch, and HNR floor per instrument class; (d) after a forced mid-chart refusal fixture: switch instrument + Play must recover (RC2 regression). Driver skeleton exists and is proven (scratchpad/repro-61c5/drive*.mjs — found all three root causes in one run). Wire as predeploy:playback + docs/DEPLOY_GATE.md; the ship pipeline runs it after predeploy:check.

title: Native Apple: make stored chord annotations editable and visible
description: Wire the existing JazzChordEvent.annotation field into the native chord inspector and lead-sheet surface. This closes a pure integration gap: annotations already validate, persist in canonical JSON, survive unchanged quick-entry reparses, undo/redo, and recovery, but musicians currently cannot see or edit them. Keep annotation editing local, bounded, coalesced, accessible, and honest about interchange loss.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a chord exposes an annotation editor populated from that exact event. ## Placement

  import export/playback/domain; UI may not import export, so the workflow contract that
  references E1 report/loss types must live in application; the UI half is expressed as
  view-model types the future dialog renders). Imported by nothing in production

- Doc: `docs/U7_MIDI_EXPORT_WORKFLOW_CONTRACT.md`
- Fixtures: `tests/fixtures/midi-export-workflow/` — manifest, preview-cases,
  state-cases, limit-cases, mutation-controls, trace-ledger, provenance-ledger.
- Validator: `scripts/validate-u7-contract.ts` (no src imports, restates constants,
  independently re-derives preview models; hash expectations computed from E1's pinned
  golden bytesHex so production is never consulted).
- Static test: `tests/static/u7-contract.test.ts`.

## Key laws to freeze
1. Preview binding: (documentId, revision) pinned at open; every later stage re-checks;
   stale → `u7.revision_stale`, never silent re-read.
2. Preview model: readiness; realization summary (generated/manual/frozen counts);
   PPQ 960 / tempo / meter / 2 tracks; bass policy disclosure (V0 external bass
   excluded exactly as declared); blocked events (voicing failures + E1 refusals incl.
   jcpe-u0mc duplicate-unison, linked, capped at MAX_DOCUMENT_CHORD_EVENTS);
   losses (E1 three kinds + U7 notice kinds); safe filename (E1 law);
   deterministic artifact hash sha256 lowercase hex over SMF bytes; byteLength.
3. Marker derivation law (U7-owned, E1 never derives text):
   - chord markers: canonical T0 symbol per event, source order;
   - section markers: section name per section-start event;
   - text > 96 UTF-8 bytes or containing control chars → marker OMITTED, event listed
     in preview as omitted-annotation (reason: text-over-limit / text-control-chars) —
     disclosed omission, never truncation, never blocking.
   - title: empty → "Untitled"; >96 bytes → code-point-safe byte truncation WITH a
     preview notice (track-name metadata, not musical data; disclosed).
   - voicingTrackName "Voicings", instrumentName pinned literal.
4. Generate: exportMidi on the compiled current-revision plan; any E1 refusal surfaces
   as a blocked preview (u7.export_refused carrying the E1 code); no partial bytes.

   discipline, restated); synchronous activation start; object-URL cleanup laws
   restated from accepted E0 (structural equality pinned by static test, E0 v1 pins
   unchanged — additive idiom); MIDI delivery binding kind "standard-midi-file";
   MIDI export NEVER touches the canonical lastExport marker and NEVER calls recovery
   Save; cancellation/failure advances nothing.
6. Dialog state machine (closed set): idle → preview-open → generating → ready →
   delivering → delivered; cancel/close from every non-delivering state; stale detected
   at generate and at delivery-take; failure states with cleanup outcomes; re-preview
   from stale. Focus/live-region matrix per state (open focus target, announcement
   text keys, Escape behavior, focus return on close).
7. Accessibility state matrix: per state × surface (dialog ≥768px / sheet <768px):
   initial focus, live-region politeness+key, allowed actions, focus-return-on-close.

   hashed) with limits from P0/E1 caps.

u7.request_invalid, u7.document_unavailable, u7.revision_stale,
u7.realization_blocked, u7.plan_refused, u7.export_refused, u7.hash_unavailable,

  cleanup-failed; single-use second-take refused; re-preview after stale.
- LIM: 96/97-byte marker text boundary; title truncation boundary; blocked list cap;
  preparation id bounds; state-matrix completeness.
- MUT: pointer corruptions (~16).
- Trace: every bead requirement row → cases + named future owners

description:
## Background
This is reviewed plan package E1 in the Advanced Craft milestone and implements a selected deterministic Idea Wizard capability.

## Required implementation
Write deterministic Standard MIDI File type 1 at PPQ 960: conductor tempo/meter/markers plus per-part voicing tracks from P0 and V2. Preserve exact ticks, gates, velocity, ordering, bass policy, Manual/Frozen pitches, and source trace diagnostics. Report nearest-microsecond tempo conversion and explicit spelling/annotation losses.

## Invariants and risks
Consume the shared playback plan; never reparse symbols, revoice, silently quantize, export stale state, or depend on a CDN. SMF headers, chunks, VLQs, running status, track counts, and byte order are deterministic.

## Success criteria
Bytes parse independently as valid SMF-1 and reproduce the expected tick/event model for dense chords, rests, meters, sections, gates, bass, and all PPQ-integral durations.

## Test plan and detailed logging
Independent minimal SMF parser and golden hashes; headers/chunks/VLQ/running-status, 2/2 through 6/8, BPM bounds, Manual/Frozen, external bass, loss report, stale/missing realization, filenames and object-URL cleanup. Log stable identities, inputs, limits, termination and exact diffs without leaking chart content unnecessarily.

## Non-goals
No MIDI import, live device access, General MIDI sound claim, microtonal pitch bends, or UI. Preserve unrelated work.

title: G3: Goal-directed Harmonic Route Planner
description:
## Background
This is reviewed plan package G3 in the Advanced Craft milestone and implements a selected deterministic Idea Wizard capability.

## Required implementation
Search lawful routes of at most 8 events and 64 outgoing candidates per state between validated endpoints. Accept context, law/evidence tiers, pins, length/rhythm/range and ranking constraints. Use fixed-work-quanta search capped at 50,000 states and 64 MiB. Return exact symbols/realizations, proof chain, evidence/counterevidence, cost vector, voice motion, identity, stats, termination and nonmutating patch.

## Invariants and risks
No runtime AI, wall-time semantic cutoff, probability theater, hidden relaxation or unlabeled enharmonic reinterpretation. Revalidate source revision before Apply; zero/capped results remain explicit and useful.

## Success criteria
Small graphs match exhaustive Pareto routes; endpoints and hard constraints always hold; resume/yield schedules are byte-identical and route identities dedupe stably.

## Test plan and detailed logging
Tonicization, secondary dominant, tritone substitution, modal interchange, diminished/common-tone pivots, ambiguity, unreachable endpoints, pins, all caps, cancellation/resume, stale Apply, transposition/metamorphic laws and browser responsiveness logs. Log stable identities, inputs, limits, termination and exact diffs without leaking chart content unnecessarily.

## Non-goals
No free-form composition model, melody generator, universal best-route claim, or UI. Preserve unrelated work.

title: G4: Constraint Harmonization Workbench engine
description:
## Background
This is reviewed plan package G4 in the Advanced Craft milestone and implements a selected deterministic Idea Wizard capability.

## Required implementation
Compile typed melody, bass, chord, rhythm, range, style and endpoint constraints into legal candidates via T1/G0/G2/V2. Support 16 slots, 128 candidates per slot and 100,000 states with fixed work quanta. Separate hard constraints from soft cost axes; return Pareto solutions or actionable conflict sets, stats, termination and exact revision-checked patch.

## Invariants and risks
Never invent coverage for an impossible note, silently reinterpret spelling, relax pins, merge hard/soft requirements, mutate during search, or confuse literal identity with contextual reading.

## Success criteria
Small spaces equal brute-force enumeration; every solution satisfies every hard constraint; unsatisfiable cases identify the actual conflicting slots/rules; cancellation/resume/yield order is deterministic.

## Test plan and detailed logging
Independent brute-force oracle; melody/bass/spelling near misses, contradictory pins, exact rhythm, Manual/Frozen, plural/no context, 16/128/100k bounds, memory counters, transposition, ties, cancellation, stale patch and performance observation. Log stable identities, inputs, limits, termination and exact diffs without leaking chart content unnecessarily.

## Non-goals
No audio transcription, melody extraction, probabilistic inference, or UI. Preserve unrelated work.

title: G8: Motif, sequence, and nonfunctional transformation atlas
description:
## Background
This is reviewed plan package G8 in the Advanced Craft milestone and implements selected deterministic Idea Wizard capabilities.

## Required implementation
Extract typed motifs and generate bounded diatonic, chromatic and intervallic sequences with exact target landings, spelling policy, rhythm preservation and proof chain. Add explicitly limited common-tone, planing, chromatic-mediant and neo-Riemannian P/L/R laws on eligible triads with preserved tones, exact voice motion and refusal outside domain.

## Invariants and risks
Do not infer motifs from arbitrary repetition, apply P/L/R to seventh/custom/unsupported sonorities, overclaim functional explanation, lose enharmonic rationale or ignore landing/range/measure constraints. Every variant passes normal parser/resolver/validation laws.

## Success criteria
Transforms land exactly or refuse, preserve declared rhythm/common tones, state relation/domain/limitations, dedupe by stable identity and obey declared transpose/inverse laws.

## Test plan and detailed logging
Motif false positives; diatonic/chromatic sequences and landing failures; meters/ranges; P/L/R truth tables and ineligible near misses; common-tone/planing/mediant goldens, spelling alternatives, inverse/metamorphic/transposition, deterministic bounds and mutation tests. Log identities, evidence, limits, termination and exact diffs.

## Non-goals
No Schenkerian-analysis claim, arbitrary graph embedding, style imitation, or UI. Preserve unrelated work.

Generate bounded seeded chart-derived exercises for spelling, chord roles, guide tones, voice leading, context, cadence/law recognition, constrained completion, reharmonization comparison and finite playback/listening questions. Record seed/engine/content/source versions and grade exact allowed answers with itemized arithmetic rubrics.

title: H0: Implement evidence-tier context readings and chord-scale tables
description:
## Background
This is reviewed plan package H0 in Musical Intelligence. It expands the trusted editor with deterministic, evidence-bearing theory rather than opaque recommendation.

## Required implementation
Implement literal/context boundary, KeyContext readings, exact diatonic/chromatic Roman labels, ordinary vs secondary/applied dominants, secondary leading-tone, tritone/backdoor, mixture, passing diminished, ambiguous/unclassified outcomes, and versioned rule/evidence tiers. Implement normative chord-match weights and explicit chord-scale/tension mapping table for Ionian/Lydian/Mixolydian/Lydian dominant/altered/whole-tone/diminished/Dorian/melodic-minor/Locrian families with containment, clash, exceptions, citations, and near misses.

Every mapping/rule has independent positive and adversarial near-miss rows across roots; evidence-tier derivation is deterministic; no-key/modal/nonfunctional spans remain legitimate; mutations of targets/spellings/tiers fail.

Conformance/golden tests for the normative tables including D7→G/A7→Dm/C7→F/Db7→C near misses, all modes/roots, altered realizations, minor-ninth clashes, suspended exceptions, absent key, ambiguity, and independently authored authority ledger entries.

title: Epic: Reliable Studio — author, recover, import, play, and stop
description:
## Background
This milestone turns the trustworthy core into a real progression editor and eliminates the legacy data-loss, touch, transport, preview, and stale-audio failures.

## Goals
- Command/history state with stable-ID selection and transactional replacement.
- Recovery, canonical/legacy import/export, lead-sheet chart editing, inspector, piano.
- Exact local voicing and playback plans.
- One lazy persistent Web Audio graph with serialized transport and strict no-future-attack Stop.
- Responsive accessible shell, real preview, transport, and lifecycle dialogs.

## Included plan packages
A0, A1, C0, P0, V0, X0, X1, E0, U0, U1, U2, U4, U5.

## Guardrails
No UI calls audio/storage directly; no import applies before confirmation; manual/custom pitches remain exact; preview is nonmutating; document replacement retires all audio generations before publish; all UI/audio integration waits on X1 stop-safety.

## Epic exit
A user can create/edit/reorder/undo/recover/migrate/import/export JSON or chart text and reliably preview/play/pause/seek/stop/replay on keyboard, pointer, and touch, with failure E2E and no stale audio.

title: A0: Implement application commands, history, bookmarks, and selectors
description:
## Background
This is reviewed plan package A0 in the Reliable Studio milestone. It must eliminate a documented legacy failure class while preserving the Foundation contracts.

## Required implementation
Create explicit AppState and pure reducer/command runner over ValidatedDocument. Implement stable-ID selection, insertion, range, dialog/panel/draft/notices, revision/export state, derived selectors, and HistoryEntry with before/after documents plus selection/insertion/range bookmarks. Cover insert/delete/move/duration/section/chord/voicing/transpose/suggestion/New/lesson/import commands, coalescing rules, 200-entry/16 MiB cap, redo clearing, focus repair, and deterministic failure.

## Invariants and risks
TransportViewState is only a generation-tagged projection of the authoritative service. Audio/playhead are not history. Commands validate isolated results before publish; no JSON clone, index identity, partial mutation, stale async result, or undisclosed oversized-replacement undo loss.

## Success criteria
All mutations are atomic/reversible within the disclosed cap; imports/replacements restore exact bookmarks; stale requests cannot publish; selectors never cache into document data; stable identity survives reorder/duplicate/undo/redo.

## Test plan and detailed logging
Integration/property tests for every command/inverse, coalescing boundaries, eviction, import undo/redo, ID collisions, selection/focus after deletion/reorder, stale request IDs, old transport notifications, and 1,000 randomized edit/undo sequences with seed/action log.

## Non-goals
Do not substitute mocks where this package names real adapters/audio/browser behavior, and do not weaken exact musical/data semantics to make UI integration easier. Preserve unrelated work.

notes:
PROGRESS CHECKPOINT 10 (2026-07-25, agent FoggyDeer). Byte ceiling unblocked, the insertion-plan notice landed, and a draft-targeting inconsistency was fixed. Read checkpoint 9 first; this is additive to it.

## The byte ceiling is no longer the constraint
The owner chose identifier minification over spending the Atlas reservation. scripts/build.ts now passes --minify-identifiers. Artifact 1,041,445 -> 752,096 bytes on that change alone; a 289,349-byte (27.8%) reduction with foundationShellMaxBytes, reservedAtlasBytes and maxUncompressedBytes all UNCHANGED, so D0's 512 KiB reservation was not touched. Tracked and closed as jcpe-siz4.
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md previously said 'The identifier-preserving inspectable bundle policy is deliberate and unchanged.' That was a real documented policy, not an oversight. It is now explicitly WITHDRAWN in a new section giving the measurement and stating what the reversal does not cost (reproducibility, the embedded CSP hashes, manifest auditability) and what it does (reading the release bundle directly, never a release requirement). Recording it rather than quietly contradicting it.

## U1-CMP-007 InsertionPlanNotice
previewInsertionPlan() states exactly one of the five statements for the current draft and target, and dispatches nothing. It reuses completeDraftPlacement — the same chooser applyQuickEntryPreview uses — so the statement cannot drift from the dispatch. The notice renders in the quick-entry panel with its explicit resolutions, and canInsert is now driven by plan.committable, so the statement and the affordance can never disagree.

### One thing the classification got wrong first, and why
The first version returned not-atomic-refusal for a short bar, because it checked draft.status !== 'ready' before looking at anything else. In fact T0 REFUSES an underfilled bar outright with chart.bar_underfilled rather than publishing a short measure, so 'the draft leaves a short bar' is visible only in the diagnostics. A draft refused for nothing but chart.bar_underfilled is now the incomplete case; anything else is a genuine non-atomic refusal. The draft's own status is no longer consulted at all — it is a summary, and the two blocked statements need the diagnostic to be told apart. A short-bar check I had written over the parsed draft was dead code and is gone: the parser returns no draft at all in that case.

### A work-bound fix
previewInsertionPlan re-parses the draft, and calling it during render would have re-parsed on every render. U1_WORK_BOUNDS.previewTokenVisits is 'at-most-maxPreviewTokens-per-draft-change', so it is now behind a useMemo keyed on the draft text, its target, and the revision.

## A targeting inconsistency, fixed
The measure target button set bookmarks.insertion, but the quick-entry draft carries its OWN target (state.quickEntry.target), and quickEntryTarget() re-derived from the insertion bookmark on every keystroke. Aiming at a measure after typing therefore left the plan and the eventual dispatch pointed at the previous measure. Now: a draft keeps the target it was aimed at, the bookmark is only the fallback for a draft with no target, the measure button re-aims the existing draft through exactly one set-quick-entry intent (U1-OP-002), and the highlighted target reads from quickEntry.targetId. The view model gained brand-free quickEntry.target/targetId for this, mirroring rangeAnchor/rangeFocus.

## U1-OP-005 recovered-chord lane (the largest remaining gap, now closed)
`insertRecoveredChord(globalOrdinal, callerBeatText, acknowledgement, incompleteReason)` builds the A0 `RecoveredChordInsertFragmentEditPlan` and dispatches exactly one `apply-edit-plan` command. `previewQuickEntryDraft()` replaced the planned separate preview: one bounded T0 parse now answers both the token rows and the lane state, so the declared at-most-maxPreviewTokens-per-draft-change work bound still holds with the App memoising it on (draft text, target id, revision).

Token rows implement U1-CMP-004/005, which did not exist at all: a parsed draft yields one `valid` row per parsed event; a refused draft yields one `insertable` row per chord T0 published plus one `invalid` row per diagnostic and no `valid` rows, exactly as contract 4 requires. Every row's `sourceText` is the exact draft slice taken from T0's own source range; nothing is repaired, canonicalised, or guessed.

The A0 plan type pins `layoutLossAcknowledgement` to the literal, so a typed caller cannot construct a wrong one and `edit-plan.recovered-chord-layout-loss-unacknowledged` is unreachable from U1. Rather than fabricate that A0 refusal, the surface carries the literal from a checkbox the caller ticks into the controller call, and the controller refuses `u1.quick_entry_lane_mismatch` when what arrives is not the literal — 4.2 states the acknowledgement as a precondition *of the lane*, so a request without it is not a recovered-chord request. A resolved T0 duration must fit the destination remainder; a `requires-caller` duration needs a positive remainder plus exact caller beat text. Supplying a duration for a chord T0 already resolved refuses `u1.duration_invalid` rather than being ignored. After the insert the destination's completion is recomputed exactly by the same `completionAfterEdit` the other edits use: exact fill publishes `complete`, a short bar refuses `u1.completion_reason_required` and routes through the measure-completion dialog, and an overfill refuses `u1.duration_overfills_measure`. ## Contract 5.3 dirty-draft prompt
Switching away from an inline symbol editor holding a draft that differs from the chord's stored text now records the interrupted transition verbatim (`DeferredSwitch`) and prompts Apply, Discard, or Continue editing. ## Nine declared key bindings were missing or wrong
`U1_KEY_BINDINGS` is a closed table; the implementation honoured 29 of its 38 rows. Fixed: Alt+M was bound to move-following (U1-OP-013, whose declared access is a menu item) instead of move-to-boundary (U1-OP-012); Alt+K, Alt+L, Alt+C and Alt+B (split-section, join-sections, set-measure-completion, set-section-boundary) did nothing at all; the range scope had no Home, End or Escape. `declareMeasureCompletion(measureId, reason)` was added for Alt+C: it publishes the completion the measure's own exact fill implies. On a measure whose stored completion already matches, A0 refuses `command.payload_invalid` and U1 surfaces that verbatim rather than rewriting it into a U1 code.

## Three defects found and fixed while proving this

2. The range bar rendered `Range ? to ? beats` whenever the two edges were the same boundary, because `selectBeatRange` correctly returns null for a span of no beats. It now says so instead of printing question marks; it still never invents a beat label.
3. The measure-completion dialog first opened from a button inside the refusal notice. The U0 `Dialog` restores focus to its declared trigger, and a successful Confirm removes the refusal — so every successful declaration raised `ui.stale_owner` and dropped focus to the workspace fallback. The dialog now names the chart region as its owner, which outlives every notice, and it opens by itself when an operation is interrupted by a reason-required refusal. title: U1/verify: Prove conformance, integration, and evidence
description:
## Package contract carried into this task
### U1: Build quick entry and stable-ID lead-sheet chart editing

## Background
This is reviewed plan package U1 in the Reliable Studio milestone. It must eliminate a documented legacy failure class while preserving the Foundation contracts.

## Required implementation
Implement QuickEntry raw draft/parsed preview/token errors, whole-chart atomic apply and explicit one-token insertion; semantic chart with sections/measures/chord cards/insertion targets; select/shift range/touch Set Start-End; inline valid-on-Apply symbol edit; insert/duplicate/delete/move/split/join/duration/section operations; optional pointer drag plus complete keyboard/menu alternatives; stable roving focus; measure fit/split/rebalance/incomplete confirmation; compact/teaching views.

## Invariants and risks
Touch preventDefault only after real drag threshold; component listeners/pointer capture clean up once. Selection/insertion/range/playhead remain distinct. Blur never coerces invalid text. No index keys, beat loss, hidden rests, silent rebalance, or drag-required authoring.

## Success criteria
Desktop/mobile/keyboard/touch users can author/reorder/range/edit charts with correct focus/IDs/history/measure timing; parse errors and all empty/overfill states are clear; listener counts stay constant.

## Test plan and detailed logging
E2E quick entry/chart/touch/reorder/focus/range/measure workflows at named viewports, property tests for stable-ID commands, repeated mount/reorder listener counts, pointer cancel/unmount, text errors, Delete+Undo, and L-TOUCH/L-STATE regressions with action/focus logs.

## Non-goals
Do not substitute mocks where this package names real adapters/audio/browser behavior, and do not weaken exact musical/data semantics to make UI integration easier. Preserve unrelated work.

## This subtask
Independently verify the implemented package against every named success criterion and test case above. Complete the package-specific unit/property/metamorphic/golden/mutation/integration/browser/audio/accessibility/performance evidence that applies; use real adapters whenever the contract names them. Exercise positive, near-miss, refusal, limit, cancellation, resume, stale revision, cleanup, and deterministic replay paths with detailed reproducible logs.

## Deliverables
- The complete named test suite and machine-readable logs/snapshots/hashes/counters.
- A trace ledger showing every parent requirement, invariant, success criterion, and legacy/Idea-Wizard regression has evidence.
- Reviewed baselines and explicit limitations only where the parent contract permits them.
- Targeted fixes plus regression tests for defects found during verification.

## Exit criteria
All package gates are green from a clean invocation, no unexplained retry/skip/quarantine exists, no serious console/leak/nondeterminism issue remains, and the evidence is sufficient to close the parent package. Record commands, versions, seeds, environment and concise results in the bead closeout.
notes:
PROGRESS CHECKPOINT 2 (2026-07-26, agent SwiftStone). The leaf's four remaining bodies of work are done: every operation-matrix row is driven, the interaction matrix is driven except four cases blocked on packages U1 does not own, all 18 laws now carry executed evidence on both polarities, and the three-browser matrix runs for the first time.

## The WebKit blocker is gone

WebKit could not launch on this host. Playwright's own dependency check named `libicu74`, but that was only the part it could map to a package: the shipped `minibrowser-gtk/bin/MiniBrowser` and `minibrowser-wpe/bin/MiniBrowser` also needed `libjxl.so.0.8` and `libbacktrace.so.0`, none of which exist in Ubuntu 25.10 (questing ships ICU 76 and libjxl 0.11).

Resolved without weakening anything: `libbacktrace0` from the distro, `libicu74` extracted from the Ubuntu noble `.deb`, and `libjxl0.8` (0.8.2-4) from `snapshot.debian.org` with its published SHA-1 verified (`c1c988354228bd71045461af25b6442d1d758484`). The four ICU sonames and the two libjxl sonames were copied into the two `webkit-2311` bundle `lib/` directories, which is where Playwright already points `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. `ldd` now reports nothing missing for either MiniBrowser.

- The very first WebKit run passed 126 of 126 with no WebKit-specific defect behind the launch failure. Two defects did surface later, once the new specs exercised focus — see below; both were latent in every engine and only WebKit made them observable.

Extraction root, for reproduction: `~/.cache/ms-playwright-extra-deps/`.

## Every non-positive operation-matrix row is now driven

`tests/integration/u1-refusal-rows.test.ts` (new, 14 tests) closes the eleven rows that `u1-edit-channel.test.ts` could not reach. All 59 rows — 36 positive plus 23 non-positive — are now driven or have their unreachability measured.

`tests/support/u1-chart-fixture.ts` (new) is what makes that possible. Quick entry can only ever produce Auto voicings and can only grow a chart one publication at a time, so two families of rows were out of reach through the product's own entry path. The fixture authors a candidate document and publishes it through the same real F2 decode and F3 semantic boundary the product uses; a candidate either boundary refuses is reported as a refusal rather than forced in. A chart that already carries stored pitches is what a user reopens, so this is an ordinary document fact rather than the U2 operation the previous checkpoint assumed it needed.

- **U1-OPC-036 / U1-OPC-037** (Manual and Frozen voicing block the inline rename) now run against a real chord with real stored pitches. Both refuse `u1.symbol_edit_blocked_manual_voicing` with the revision unmoved, and a third test proves the rendered chart is byte-identical after each refusal.
- **U1-OPC-050** (a selection of exactly 8,192 chords) runs against a chart at the exact document capacity: 1,024 measures of eight eighth-notes. The extend is one `ephemeral-updated` intent, the selection holds exactly 8,192 ids, and the revision does not move.
- **U1-OPC-051** (8,193 chords refuse with `u1.selection_limit`) is **unreachable, and now provably so**: `MAX_SELECTED_EVENT_IDS` is not an independent number, it *is* `MAX_DOCUMENT_CHORD_EVENTS`. The test asserts that equality and then shows that a document holding one more event is refused by F2. The guard's refusal branch has no valid document to live in.
- **U1-OPC-052** (a T0-refused draft dispatched so A0 can answer `edit-plan.syntax-refused`) is likewise unreachable, for the opposite reason: the surface *can* see the refusal in advance. `previewInsertionPlan()` states `not-atomic-refusal` and `applyQuickEntryPreview()` refuses `u1.insertion_plan_not_atomic` before dispatch, with no command published and the draft text untouched. That is strictly stronger than the row asks for — the same shape as the U1-QE-043/044 finding in checkpoint 1.
- **U1-OPC-054** (two Duplicate activations in one frame) drives two activations with no clock tick between them: each advances the revision by exactly one and each is its own undo step. Neither batched nor nested.
- **U1-OPC-035** (`command.wrong_document`) cannot arise from this surface: `replace-document` is frozen outside the U1 command surface, so the test drives insert, duplicate, rename, insert-section, undo and redo and proves the document identity never moves. The mismatch the row needs has no U1 gesture that can create it.
- **U1-OPC-034** (a stale Delete) holds one step earlier: the Delete gesture captures no revision at all, it reads the live snapshot at dispatch. The test advances the revision out of band and shows the following Delete is the correct command against current state.
- **U1-OPC-053** (`u1.operation_not_authorized`) is proved behaviourally rather than by inspection. The six unauthorized kinds each move a value U1 must never move, so the test drives the surface hard against a chart with a Manual voicing and asserts that meter, key, tempo, instrument, volumes, count-in, document identity, the stored chord's symbol and its voicing mode are all exactly where they started.
- **U1-OPC-056 / U1-OPC-057** (pointer capture lost, and a release below the threshold) are driven in the browser — see below.

## The interaction-state matrix: 54 of 58, with the other four explained

`tests/integration/u1-interaction-states.test.ts` (new, 10 tests) covers the states whose subject is application state: U1-INT-005 (selecting never moves the insertion point, and the three bookmarks hold three different values at once while the playhead does not move), U1-INT-014 and U1-INT-015 (the declared delete-repair order, falling back to the previous event and then to the section insertion target, never to the document body), U1-INT-050 (clearing the draft is one ephemeral intent), U1-INT-051, U1-INT-052 (an out-of-band undo repairs the bookmark and publishes a focus request), and U1-INT-046/047.

`tests/e2e/u1-pointer-listeners.spec.ts` (new, 10 tests) and `tests/e2e/u1-empty-errors.spec.ts` (new, 7 tests) cover the states whose subject is the rendered surface, all against the real generated artifact: the 8 CSS-pixel threshold and the `preventDefault` that waits for it (U1-INT-017/018, U1-OPC-057), pointer cancel and mid-drag unmount (U1-OPC-056, U1-INT-020), the three transient listeners and their release (U1-INT-025), per-card listener totals across ten reorders of twenty cards (U1-INT-023), a whole authoring session on the keyboard alone (U1-INT-021), the empty chart and empty selection (U1-INT-042/045), individually visible token errors (U1-INT-043), exact beats and stored reasons (U1-INT-046/047), and clean cancellation of an inline edit and of the completion dialog (U1-INT-048/049).

The four that are **not** driven, and why:

1. **U1-INT-002** ("playback advances across three chords") and **U1-INT-003** ("a chord preview is auditioned from the card menu") need playback and audition. The studio transport reports `status: "unavailable"`, `isAvailable: false` — X0/X1 are not wired to it yet. These are blocked on those packages, not on U1.
2. **U1-INT-006** states its precondition as "playhead at beat 12". No U1 operation can move the playhead — that is exactly the law it tests — and nothing else can either until the transport is wired. Its three-bookmark half is asserted in `U1-INT-005`; its rendered-accessible-name half is not, so the case is deliberately left unlinked rather than half-claimed.
3. **U1-INT-026** ("the chart region is unmounted") has no product path: `StudioShell` mounts `ChartWorkspace` unconditionally for the lifetime of the app. The leak class it guards is covered instead by U1-INT-020 (a card unmounted mid-drag) and U1-INT-023 (per-card totals across ten reorders).

## Law coverage is complete on both polarities

The emitted ledger at `test-results/u1-evidence/trace-ledger.json` now reports **18 of 18 laws with executed evidence on both polarities**, up from 17 at the last checkpoint and 10 when the ledger was first computed. Named case ids rose from 70 to 100. Every per-law floor in `PINNED_FLOOR` was raised to the measured value, and `lawsWithBothPolarities` is now pinned at 18: coverage may rise, never fall.

Four laws still have a declared case with no executed evidence, and all four are the cases listed above: U1-EDIT-003 (19/20 negative), U1-EDIT-008 (10/13 positive), U1-EDIT-015 (3/4 positive), U1-EDIT-017 (7/8 negative).

## The browser proofs read the reviewed numbers instead of copying them

`u1-pointer-listeners.spec.ts` reads `pointerPolicy.dragThresholdCssPx`, `listenerPolicy.transientDragListenersPerSession` and `listenerPolicy.maxConcurrentDragSessions` out of the fixture packet rather than restating them as literals. That is what makes the browser proof mutation-sensitive: `U1-MUT-021` changes the threshold and `U1-MUT-024` changes the listener budget, and a private copy of those numbers here would let the production surface keep passing against a packet that no longer says what it says. The validator's own replay of all 32 controls stays green (`mutationControlsReplayed: 32`).

## Six defects found and fixed

1. **Renaming the chart after any chord edit was refused.** `setTitle` stamped its command from a private clock, `(ordinal - 1) * TITLE_COMMAND_INTERVAL_MS`, that started at zero and never saw the shared logical clock every other command advances. The first rename after any edit therefore travelled backwards in logical time and A0 refused it with `command.logical_time_invalid`. Every real session hits this — the user types changes, then names the chart. The spacing that keeps consecutive renames out of the text-coalescing window is now measured *from* the shared clock instead of replacing it, so renames are still separate undo entries with exact snapshots. Three regression tests: rename after an edit, two renames staying separate undo steps, and a rename interleaved between two edits.
2. **A card unmounted mid-drag wedged dragging permanently.** `useEffect(() => endDragSession, [])` released the session only when the whole chart region unmounted. When an undo or a delete repair removed the card a drag was holding, the detached handle could never fire `pointerup` or `pointercancel` again, so `dragSession.current` stayed set and `beginDrag` returned early on every later attempt — dragging was dead for the rest of the session. Found by driving U1-INT-020, whose "and the surface is not wedged: a fresh drag still starts" assertion failed. Now released per card when its handle leaves the document, which is the "capture is released on unmount" half of the reviewed pointer policy.
3. **An overfilling duration notice stated no numbers.** U1-INT-046 requires the exact current fill, the exact resulting fill and the capacity as rationals; the message said only "The new duration changes the measure fill and needs an explicit decision." `completionAfterEdit` now returns the exact resulting total and the capacity with its refusal, and the duration path states all three ("This measure holds 4/1 of 4/1 beats; the new duration would make it 7/1.").
4. **A short measure never showed its stored reason.** U1-INT-047 requires the declared reason to be displayed with the measure and never invented. The reason was stored in the document and dropped at the view-model boundary. `StudioMeasureViewModel` now carries `completionReason` — verbatim for `incomplete` and `pickup`, `null` otherwise — and the chart renders it as a measure fact in both views, because a stored reason is a musical fact the author supplied rather than an analysis the teaching view adds.
5. **T0 diagnostic ranges were not surfaced.** §6 requires T0 codes *and ranges* verbatim; the token row showed only the code. `StudioQuickEntryToken` now carries `diagnosticRange` and the row renders it, so a reader can find the offending characters in a long draft.
6. **The inline editors were unreachable from the keyboard, and cancelling one stranded the caret.** `autoFocus` on a dynamically inserted input is not portable. Chromium and Firefox ignored it, so F2 opened an editor the caret never entered — every keystroke went to the card underneath and the "type, then Enter" path the contract describes never worked. WebKit honoured it and then dropped focus to the **document body** when the input unmounted, so every key after a cancelled edit reached nothing at all. The same gap existed after any command: the A0 focus-request renderer was a passive `useEffect`, which runs after the browser is already free to deliver the next key, so on WebKit focus sat on the body between a move and its repair. Focus is now moved explicitly when an editor opens and returned to the owning card when it closes, and both the editor effect and the A0 focus-request renderer are `useLayoutEffect`s so the repair lands before the next event can be dispatched. Two regression tests assert both halves, and they pass identically in all three engines.

Also fixed: one order-dependent E2E. `U1-INT-021` pressed Enter into a draft the surface had not yet classified, which passed in isolation and failed once in the full Chromium run. It now waits for the Insert control to become enabled — the same signal a user waits for — before publishing, and polls for the reorder instead of asserting it instantly. It then failed once more under full-project load on a different assertion, so the whole chain was hardened: every keystroke now waits for an observable settle — focus, selection count, or dialog state — before the next one is sent, because a key delivered into a half-applied state is dropped and a dropped key is a flake rather than a finding.

## The implementation-status flip, and the part of it that is not this leaf's to make

Implement progressive Symbol/Structure/Timing/Voicing/Harmony/Motion/Notes inspector over draft AST; parse/canonical diagnostics; degree/pitch/bass/omission display; exact timing; Auto/Manual/Frozen switching with confirmation; semantic structured edits; annotation; MIDI-coordinate piano with spelling/octave/accessibility and list/spin alternative; real audio Preview through X1/X0 without selection/document/playhead mutation.

title: U0: Build accessible design tokens, primitives, and responsive studio shell
description:
## Background
This is reviewed plan package U0 in the Reliable Studio milestone. It must eliminate a documented legacy failure class while preserving the Foundation contracts.

## Required implementation
Implement system-font dark lead-sheet/studio design tokens, semantic state colors, CSS reset/layout/breakpoints, skip link/landmarks/headings, header/workspace/collapsible rails/transport shell, and small Button/IconButton/Field/Select/Segmented/Menu/Tooltip/Dialog/Sheet/Notice/Tabs/Disclosure/VisuallyHidden primitives. No CDN/fonts/icon/modal/drag/CSS runtime; no hue-only state, nested modal, browser zoom block, hover-only primary action, invalid nested buttons, or JS device guesses. UI dispatches intents/selectors only.

## Success criteria
Primitive matrix and shell visual/accessibility evidence pass every named viewport/state; serious/critical rule violations are zero or reviewed; focus/order/restoration and mobile transport remain usable.

## Test plan and detailed logging
Component/browser tests for names/roles/tab/arrow/Escape/focus return/live regions/disabled/errors, forced colors/reduced motion/zoom/320x568 through 1440x900 snapshots, mobile sheet/dialog nesting, empty/error/audio/storage states, and axe rule IDs/exceptions logging.

## Non-goals
Do not substitute mocks where this package names real adapters/audio/browser behavior, and do not weaken exact musical/data semantics to make UI integration easier. Preserve unrelated work.

## 2026-07-11 user-directed UI replacement
The legacy UI is replaced completely. Use the source-owned component-library approach popularized by shadcn, but implement it natively in Preact and CSS. Do not add React, Radix, Tailwind, shadcn packages, preact/compat, a CSS runtime, a CDN, or another production dependency.

U0 must specify and deliver a cohesive, high-polish library spanning foundations (Button/IconButton/LinkButton/Badge/Kbd/Separator/Skeleton/Spinner/VisuallyHidden/Card/EmptyState/StatusPill/Progress/Meter), forms (Field/Label/Input/Textarea/NumberField/Select/Combobox/Listbox/Checkbox/RadioGroup/Switch/Slider/SegmentedControl/Toggle/ToggleGroup), navigation/commands (Tabs/Breadcrumb/Toolbar/Menu/ContextMenu/CommandPalette/Disclosure/Accordion/ScrollArea/roving focus), overlays/feedback (Tooltip/Popover/Dialog/AlertDialog/Sheet-Drawer/Toast-Notice with one focus/dismissal layer), and structured views (KeyValueList/DataTable/Tree/ResizablePanels/timeline-lane primitives). Implement only source-owned behavior needed by planned surfaces, with stable public APIs rather than one-off feature controls.

Every meaningful component state—default, hover, active, focus, disabled, loading, error, empty, dense, responsive, forced-colors, reduced-motion, 200 percent zoom and touch—belongs in a test-only component gallery and visual/accessibility matrix. The gallery is excluded from the release artifact. Final integration receives a dedicated ui-polish pass after workflows function.

title: Mobile sheet duplicates every rail panel id while open (pre-existing, amplified by the progression library)
notes:
MEASURED 2026-07-29 on artifact 91ae9a42, Chromium 390x844.

Sheet CLOSED: 0 duplicate ids in the whole document.
Sheet OPEN (#studio-open-library-sheet): 69 duplicate ids.
  33 PRE-EXISTING: studio-quick-entry-heading, -hint, -field, -status, -insert, -clear, studio-palette-root-* (12), studio-palette-quality-* (12), studio-quick-entry-demo-* ...

Those are referenced by e2e specs and by the U0 contract/fixtures, so it is a wide pinned-digest ripple - not something to land on top of a working deploy for a currently-cosmetic defect.
