title: Shared PCM cache evicted by current recipe's limit across recipes
description:
Audit finding (2026-08-06). The shared rendered-PCM cache is evicted using whichever recipe rendered last, so a small-limit instrument evicts a large-limit instrument's legitimately cached buffers.

Evidence: src/audio/audio-engine.ts:874-887 `renderedBufferFor` bounds the SHARED cache map by the CURRENT recipe's `bufferCacheLimit` — rendering one guitar note (limit 64) evicts piano entries legitimately sized to a limit of 96. Deterministic, but violates per-recipe cache-limit intent and causes needless cold re-renders after instrument switches (audible as first-note lag).

Fix options: (a) per-recipe sub-caches each bounded by its own limit, with the existing global PCM byte ceiling (96 MiB, PHS0 limits) enforced across all; or (b) one cache with per-recipe entry counting and eviction that only evicts entries of the recipe being rendered unless the global byte ceiling is exceeded. (a) is simpler and keeps LRU tie-breaks deterministic per PHS0 section 5. Preserve deterministic LRU with stable-identity tie-break either way.

Acceptance:
- Unit test: render guitar past its limit while piano entries are warm -> piano entries survive; switching back to piano performs zero cold renders.
- Unit test: global byte ceiling still enforced across recipes (synthetic oversized entries).
- Deterministic eviction order test retained (extends the gesture-cache LRU tests from commit bd29778).
- typecheck/lint/test green.
close_reason: Replaced the shared rendered-PCM cache with per-recipe LRU caches in src/audio/audio-engine.ts: each recipe evicts only its own entries at min(recipe bufferCacheLimit, contract maximumCacheEntries); global maximumCacheEntries and maximumCachePcmBytes ceilings evict the globally least-recently-used entry via unique monotonic stamps (deterministic victim; per-map Map order remains each recipe's own LRU). ALSO FIXED a latent LRU defect the new tests exposed: the prepare path's cache-hit check used has() and never refreshed recency, so warmed-then-touched entries were evicted as if never used — both hit paths now share touchRenderedBufferEntry. Added deep-module test seam createAudioEngineWithRenderCacheLimitsForTest (mirrors createAudioEngineWithSequenceSeedForTest precedent, absent from the barrel) because real renders trim trailing silence making byte totals nondeterministic. Tests: tests/unit/audio-engine-render-cache.test.ts (3 tests: per-recipe skew + LRU refresh protection with 66 real renders proving concert-grand survives guitar-driven eviction; global entry ceiling choosing a cross-recipe globally-oldest victim; one-byte PCM ceiling forcing re-render) — 3 pass 0 fail; combined with gesture-binding file 8 pass 0 fail post-change. typecheck pass (190 files); lint clean in touched files (10 sibling-file errors noted, not mine); full local suite 3425/3427 with both failures in the concurrent sibling's tuning fixture mid-wasm-rebuild. Files: src/audio/audio-engine.ts, tests/unit/audio-engine-render-cache.test.ts, tests/unit/audio-engine-gesture-binding.test.ts.

title: Play path compiles the physical realization twice
description:
Audit finding (2026-08-06). Every play compiles the full physical realization twice on the latency-critical path.

Evidence: src/application/studio-audio.ts:468 (`prepareInstrument`) compiles the whole plan to warm buffers and attach gestures; src/audio/transport.ts:489 (`physicalGesturesForEvent`) compiles the identical plan again for its own memoized lookup. Same inputs, two full passes of per-gesture and per-segment TypeScript sha256 (src/audio/deterministic-sha256.ts). The peer's own uncommitted diff moved clock sampling after compile to protect the start margin — treating the cost as a given instead of removing half of it.

Fix: share one compiled ExpressiveRealizationPlan/PhysicalRenderPlan between prepare and transport, memoized on (plan object identity, instrumentId, sampleRateHz, compiler version). The natural home is the existing transport memo widened to be the single authority, with studio-audio consuming it through the engine/application seam that already carries gestures — respect layer rules (application may not import audio internals; go through the existing service interface). Invalidate on document replacement exactly like the current memo.

Acceptance:
- Unit test: prepare-then-play compiles exactly once (spy/counter on compilePhysicalRealization).
- No behavioral change to attached gestures (fingerprints identical before/after).
- Measured play-start latency before/after on a representative chart recorded in the close reason.
- typecheck/lint/test green.

Depends on the transport-rate bead (memo key gains the real rate) and peer-dirty transport.ts caveat.
close_reason: Single compile per play path: new memoizedPhysicalRealization in src/audio/physical-realization.ts (WeakMap keyed on the immutable plan object + revision/family/versionId/packSha/sampleRate string key; entries fall away with replaced plans, results are the same frozen objects). Both call sites switched: transport physicalGesturesForEvent and studio-audio prepareInstrument, so prepare-then-play compiles exactly once and repeat plays are memo hits. Measured (bun, median-of-20 after warmup): full compile of an 8-chord guitar chart = 12.465 ms; memo hit = 0.0012 ms; the play path previously paid the full compile twice (prepare + transport) per play. New tests/unit/physical-realization-memo.test.ts: identical requests return the identical frozen object (===), each render-affecting field change compiles separately, distinct plan objects never share entries, memoized === direct results by deep equality. Gates: bun --bun test across memo+fingerprint+rate+realization+transport-instrument+physical-audio-path+phs0-conformance = 51 pass 0 fail; typecheck exit 0; lint outcome pass findings []. Deviation: instead of widening the transport memo into a cross-layer authority (bead's sketch), the memo lives beside the compiler in the audio layer and both existing call sites consume it - same single-compile outcome with no new application-to-audio surface.

title: Gesture excitation bridge erases bottom third of dynamic range
description:
Audit finding (2026-08-06 fresh-eyes review, TS audio-layer auditor). The gesture excitation bridge erases the bottom ~1/3 of the dynamic range for every physical instrument.

Evidence: src/audio/physical-realization.ts:159 maps velocity to air/pick pressure as `0.35 + v/127*0.65`, and audio-engine.ts `physicalGestureExcitationVelocity` (~:426-446 consumption path) inverts that via `round(peak*127)` to feed the v1 WASM `renderNote(midi, excitationVelocity, ...)`. Result: played velocity 1 renders as excitation ~45, velocity 64 as ~86. The legacy non-gesture path kept the full 1..127 range (21-band quantized), so the gesture path is dynamically WORSE than legacy — exactly the "normalization suppresses physically meaningful dynamics" regression target frozen in docs/PHYSICAL_SYNTHESIS_PLAN.md section 3.2 and forbidden by section 6.4.

Fix: make the round trip identity-preserving. Either (a) carry the source MIDI velocity alongside the gesture and use it directly for v1 excitation (curves remain for future v2 consumption), or (b) make the pressure mapping and its inverse exact bijections over 1..127. Option (a) is simpler and honest: the curve is policy for v2; v1 excitation should not be laundered through it. Do NOT change legal curve ranges (contract-frozen Q16.16 values).

Acceptance:
- Unit test: for every velocity 1..127 and every physical family, the excitation velocity that reaches the renderer equals the plan event velocity (or documented exact bijection).
- Regression: soft (v=20) vs loud (v=110) renders of the same pitch differ in RMS and spectral centroid at least as much as the legacy non-gesture path (measure via existing analyzer exports).
- bun typecheck/lint/test green; do not touch curve validation laws.

Coordination: physical-realization.ts currently carries uncommitted peer work (jcpe-mnsc.2.3 verify). Re-check git status and mtimes before editing; if still dirty, coordinate or wait for the peer to land.
close_reason: Fixed the v1 compatibility bridge to preserve authoritative source velocity instead of converting Q16 physical operating-point floors into MIDI excitation. Proof: all 127 velocities across clarinet/flute/guitar/trumpet/vibraphone round-trip exactly; measured C4 clean-guitar v20/v110 output has RMS and spectral-centroid contrast at least the legacy v22/v106 render buckets; focused PHS0/transport suite passed. typecheck, narrow eslint, and diff check passed.

title: Canonical length-prefixed gesture/segment fingerprint serialization
description:
Audit finding (2026-08-06). Gesture/segment fingerprint serialization has structural ambiguity; PHS0 requires PROVEN collision resistance and today it rests on lexical luck.

Evidence: src/audio/physical-realization.ts:163-180 (`stableGestureText`) and :696-713 (segment identity) flatten nested curves/points with a single U+001F unit-separator character, no length prefixes, no curve delimiters — curve boundaries are implied only by control-ID enum tokens not looking like numbers. True today; one future control ID or negative-offset format change away from a real collision. PHS0 contract section 5 says the fingerprint includes every render-affecting field and demands mutation-proven collision resistance.

Fix: replace the flat join with an unambiguous canonical serialization: length-prefix each curve and each point list (element counts before elements) or hash the canonical JSON of a stable shape. Must remain deterministic and allocation-cheap (it runs per gesture on the play path — coordinate with the cache-storm and double-compile beads so hashing runs once).

Acceptance:
- Mutation tests: two structurally different gestures that would collide under the OLD flat-join scheme produce different fingerprints under the new scheme (construct the boundary case explicitly).
- All existing fingerprint identity/LRU tests updated: same input -> same hash, any render-affecting field change -> different hash.
- Cache-compat note: fingerprints all change once; caches are session-scoped so this is harmless — verify no fingerprint is persisted anywhere before closing.
- typecheck/lint/test green.

Coordination: peer-dirty physical-realization.ts caveat.
close_reason: Replaced ambiguous flat U+001F fingerprint joins with canonical length-prefixed/count-prefixed framing (schema tag phs0.fingerprint.v2) in stableGestureText and segment identity (src/audio/physical-realization.ts). New tests/unit/physical-fingerprint-canonical.test.ts proves: constructed structure pair collides under reimplemented legacy flat join (identical sha256) and is distinguished under the new framing; identity stability; per-field mutation sensitivity (11 fields); segment fingerprint determinism+sensitivity through production compiler. No fingerprint hex pinned anywhere (searched tests+fixtures); no fingerprint persisted outside audio layer (grep src/application src/persistence src/export clean). Gates: bun --bun test fingerprint+realization 11 pass; phs0 conformance+physical-audio-path+gesture-binding 33 pass; scripts/validate-phs0-contract.ts findings []; typecheck exit 0 (after fixing two pre-existing unrelated TS4111 in committed tests/static/phs1-contract.test.ts, noted as courtesy fix); lint findings [].

title: Engine never validates gesture voiceId or instrumentVersionId at attack
description:
Audit finding (2026-08-06). Gesture-to-voice binding is under-validated at the attack boundary: a gesture can be attached to the wrong voice of the right event, or carry a stale instrument version, and still render.

Evidence: src/audio/audio-engine.ts:426-446 validates `gesture.eventId === eventId` and instrument family, but never checks `gesture.voiceId` against the voice spec being attacked, and never checks `gesture.instrumentVersionId` against the active recipe's version. Swapped gestures across voices of one chord (different pick.position / strike curves per pitchOrdinal) validate silently; after an instrument hot-swap a stale-version gesture still renders.

Fix: extend the engine-side gesture validation to require (1) voice correspondence — the gesture's voiceId must match the voice spec identity derived for that pitchOrdinal, and (2) instrumentVersionId equality with the active recipe version. On mismatch, refuse the gesture with the existing named-diagnostic path (render proceeds gestureless — same behavior as today's family mismatch), never silently accept. This is the PHS0 contract validation-order law (doc section 3, steps 3 and 2) applied at the last trust boundary.

Acceptance:
- Unit tests: (pos) matching gesture accepted; (near-miss) same event, sibling voiceId -> refused with named code; (near-miss) correct voice, stale instrumentVersionId -> refused; (mutation) both wrong -> refused, deterministic diagnostic order.
- Integration: existing transport-instrument tests still green.
- typecheck/lint/test green.

title: Gesture fingerprints defeat the rendered-PCM cache (per-note cold renders)
description:
Audit finding (2026-08-06). The gesture cache fingerprint defeats the PCM render cache, turning warm playback into per-note cold synchronous main-thread renders.

Evidence: src/audio/physical-realization.ts `curvesFor` embeds `event.gateDurationTicks` (attack/duration points), `event.ordinal` (pick-direction parity and `fan.phase = ordinal%8/8`), and `pitchOrdinal` (`pick.position`) into curve points. audio-engine.ts:811-822 `renderedBufferKey` includes the gesture fingerprint. So two notes of the same pitch/velocity with different durations or ordinals get different fingerprints and both cold-render, where the legacy key (pitch x 21-velocity-band x secondsBucket) hit constantly. A 32-bar chart can force per-note cold renders (~seconds of main-thread stall at 96 kHz) where v1 did about a dozen.

Fix: quantize render-affecting gesture inputs before fingerprinting, mirroring the legacy bucketing that is already accepted policy: duration -> the existing secondsBucket; pick direction -> keep (it is only 2 values, cheap); drop ordinal-derived fan.phase from the fingerprint for instruments whose renderer ignores it today (concert-vibes consumes no gestures — see the vibraphone family-map bead); pitchOrdinal pick.position -> quantize to a small set (e.g. 8 steps). The QUANTIZED curves must be what is both fingerprinted AND rendered, so cache identity stays honest (PHS0 contract section 5: fingerprint includes every render-affecting field — quantization must happen upstream of both).

Acceptance:
- Unit test: two same-pitch/velocity events with different gateDurationTicks in the same seconds-bucket produce identical fingerprints; different buckets differ.
- Unit test: repeated quarter-note comping pattern (16 events, 4 distinct pitch/velocity pairs) performs at most len(distinct)x(buckets) cold renders (instrument-level counter already observable via render cache size).
- Measured before/after cold-render count on a representative chart recorded in the close reason.
- Existing gesture-fingerprint identity/LRU tests (bd29778) updated, not weakened: identity still changes when a render-affecting input changes.

Coordination: peer-dirty file physical-realization.ts — same caveat as the dynamics-floor bead. Depends on the vibraphone family-map decision for the fan.phase question.

POLISH ROUND 1: precise fragmentation drivers, re-derived: `fan.phase = ordinal%8/8` is already bounded (8 values) and pick parity is 2 values — the UNBOUNDED drivers are gateDurationTicks (attack/duration curve points) and per-chord pitchOrdinal pick.position. So the core fix is duration -> secondsBucket quantization plus pick.position -> small step set; the bounded controls may stay. Cross-link: jcpe-dsp-vibrato-variation-zhif adds a seeded variation-slot index (bounded, mod-8/16) to the key — design the quantized fingerprint so the slot composes with it rather than multiplying unboundedly.
close_reason: Replaced false per-event gesture-fingerprint PCM identity with exact ABI-v1 consumed identity: instrument/pitch/exact source velocity/duration bucket plus physical family+version. Curves, event IDs, and seeds remain in the immutable plan fingerprint but no longer cause cold renders until a native renderer consumes them. Measured representative result: 16 guitar comp attacks over 4 pitch/velocity pairs now produce 4 renders and 12 cache hits; 65 metadata/seed variants at one render point produce 1 render and 64 hits. Exact-velocity 65-entry sequence still proves deterministic 64-entry LRU. 18 focused tests, typecheck, eslint, diff check passed.

title: Transport compiles physical realization at hardcoded 48 kHz
description:
Audit finding (2026-08-06). Transport compiles the physical realization at a fictional hardcoded sample rate.

Evidence: src/audio/transport.ts:499 passes `sampleRateHz: 48_000` to compilePhysicalRealization while the engine renders at the real `context.sampleRate` (44.1k is common on consumer hardware). Today only tick-domain curve data is consumed downstream, so the wrong rate is latent — but the compiled segments' `timelineStartFrame`, `frameCount`, and per-segment `cacheFingerprint` are all wrong for a 44.1 kHz context the moment anything reads them (PHS0 v2 rendering will). A code comment acknowledges the lie without fencing it.

Fix: thread the actual engine/context sample rate into the transport's compile call (the engine already knows it; expose via the existing engine contract rather than a new UI-visible surface). If the rate is unavailable at compile time, compile rate-independent gestures only and defer segment lowering — but do NOT leave a wrong-rate plan where v2 consumption can reach it. Add an explicit refusal if a compiled plan's sampleRateHz mismatches the render context at consumption time (cheap invariant check at the attack boundary).

Acceptance:
- Unit test: transport-compiled plan carries the platform/context rate (44.1k and 96k cases).
- Near-miss test: consuming a plan whose sampleRateHz differs from the context refuses with a named code rather than rendering.
- typecheck/lint/test green; existing transport gesture memoization still keyed correctly (rate joins the memo key).

Coordination: transport.ts is peer-dirty (jcpe-mnsc.2.3). Wait or coordinate before editing.
close_reason: Transport and studio-audio prepareInstrument now compile the physical realization at the engine's real context sample rate (platform.engine.inspectAudioEngine().contextSampleRate) instead of hardcoded 48_000; the transport memo is additionally keyed by rate (physicalLookupSampleRateHz) so a context change recompiles. Rates outside the v2 closed set {44100,48000,96000} (and a null pre-initialization context) compile no plan rather than a lying one, via new exported type guard isPhysicalSupportedSampleRateHz in physical-renderer-contract.ts. New tests/unit/transport-sample-rate.test.ts: segments carry the requested rate at 44.1k/96k through the production compiler, and full transport harness runs at 44.1k and 96k attach one compiled gesture per physical voice (harness gained an additive sampleRate option). title: Amend plan: piano sustain-pedal sympathetic resonance package
description:
Plan omission (2026-08-06 fresh-eyes review). The concert-grand piano — the studio's flagship instrument — is entirely absent from the physical-synthesis plan, and it has NO sustain-pedal or sympathetic string resonance: nothing shares energy across notes, so pedaled jazz comping renders dry and disconnected. The plan's coupled-stem machinery (PHS0 section 4.3) is being built for guitar/vibes; the piano is its third and musically most important customer.

Evidence: dsp/concert-grand/src/lib.rs cg_* piano is 24-partial-per-string additive with per-note state only; no damper model, no inter-note coupling; auditor realism rank C6. The vibraphone package (jcpe-mnsc.8) already specifies pedal/damper contact and shared resonance across notes — the piano case is architecturally identical (pedal state + shared resonant field + per-note dampers).

Proposal to specify (additive package, sequenced AFTER PHS6 proves the pedal/coupled-stem pattern):
1. A shared "string field" stem: when the (future) sustain-pedal state is down, struck-note energy excites a bounded modal field representing undamped strings (compact: one field of N reviewed modes, not 88 full string models), fed by a fraction of each note's bridge energy; released notes decay into it.
2. Damper model per note: pedal up = current behavior (fast per-note release); pedal down = note tail transitions into the shared field.
3. Pedal state source: the playback plan has no pedal events today — specify the deterministic derivation (e.g. legato/overlap-driven auto-pedal policy in the expressive realization layer, the same layer that already derives articulation) so no domain/MIDI change is required (plan law: physical performance data is additive, MIDI must not depend on it).
4. Fixtures: strike C3 with pedal-down policy active, measure energy at E3/G3/C4 string-field modes after the C3 damper would have killed a dry note; A/B dry-vs-pedal decay slopes; determinism and Stop (field must obey serialized Stop like every source).

Acceptance: a reviewed plan amendment adding the piano-resonance package with spec/build/verify children AFTER PHS6 (dependency: proven pedal/stem pattern), plus the auto-pedal realization-policy spec. This bead is the amendment + specification outline only.

title: Specify stereo placement, source width, shared early-reflection block
description:
Plan omission (2026-08-06 fresh-eyes review). The plan specifies radiation per instrument but has NO cross-cutting treatment of stereo placement, source width, directivity, or a shared air/space model — yet "sounds like a real instrument" is judged on headphones where a bone-dry mono point source reads as synthetic regardless of model quality. This is among the cheapest remaining perceived-realism wins and it is currently nobody's bead.

Proposal to specify (deterministic, offline, cheap — feeds PHS7 and X0 amendment, NOT a per-instrument concern):
1. Per-instrument static stage placement: azimuth/width/distance constants in the recipe registry (piano wide, bass slightly left-of-center, winds center-right etc. — reviewed constants, user-visible only as a natural default image; NO new UI).
2. Source width via decorrelated dual-channel rendering where the model already computes stereo (finalize_stereo exists) — replace identical-channel duplication with a deterministic decorrelation (e.g. per-channel allpass chains with instrument-seeded coefficients), bounded inter-channel coherence targets per instrument (measured fixture).
3. A single shared early-reflection block for the whole mix (NOT per note): 4-8 deterministic taps + gentle air-absorption lowpass, one instance on the existing persistent-graph master path, coefficients reviewed and fixed. No convolution, no per-note cost, Stop guarantee untouched (tail < 80 ms).
4. Explicit non-goals: no reverb tail (release scope), no HRTF, no user-adjustable room, no per-note graph nodes (X0 one-persistent-graph law).
5. Fixtures: inter-channel coherence per instrument within authored bounds; mono-sum colouration bounded (no comb disasters — mono downmix deviation < authored dB envelope); determinism (bit-identical renders); Stop-to-silence timing unchanged (X1 law).

Acceptance: a reviewed spec section (plan amendment + X0 contract addendum) with the fixture list above; owner listening rubric rows added for with/without A-B; implementation lands as its own leaf after the spec is accepted. Keep honest: this is production/mix realism, not physics — label it accordingly in the plan (it complements, never substitutes for, the physical models; forbidden-shortcut law "do not equate more effects with realism" applies to how it is described).
close_reason: Added the cross-cutting 'Stage image and shared air' section to docs/PHYSICAL_SYNTHESIS_PLAN.md between sections 12 and 13 (non-numeric heading, no renumbering): placement constants, decorrelated width with coherence targets, single shared early-reflection master block gated on an X0 contract amendment with Stop tail <80ms, explicit non-goals, fixture list (coherence/mono-sum/determinism/Stop), owner A/B listening rows. Framed honestly as production realism complementing physics per section 17.

title: Amend plan: ukulele + physical upright bass in plucked-string family
description:
Plan omission (2026-08-06 fresh-eyes review). The owner's explicit goal is modeling the physical SIZE and SHAPE differences between instruments — "a uke versus a Martin Dreadnought style acoustic guitar, versus a huge upright bass" (owner request, 2026-08-06). docs/PHYSICAL_SYNTHESIS_PLAN.md covers a guitar family (archtop, Martin-style, Strat-style, twang, drive) but contains NO ukulele and NO physical upright bass; the bass remains sampled-only (upright-bass CC0 samples) and ukulele appears nowhere in the registry or plan.

Work (specification amendment feeding PHS4, not a freestanding build):
1. Amend PHYSICAL_SYNTHESIS_PLAN.md section 10 from "guitar family" to "plucked-string family" and add two named targets with honest per-body physical parameter sets:
   - Ukulele: ~0.33-0.38 m scale, 4 nylon strings (g4 C4 E4 A4 re-entrant option decided in spec), small body -> high Helmholtz resonance (~500-700 Hz region), low modal density, fast decay, bright low-sustain character.
   - Upright bass: ~1.04-1.06 m scale, 4 thick steel/gut-hybrid strings (E1 A1 D2 G2), huge body -> low Helmholtz (~60-100 Hz), long sustain, strong low-mode radiation, pizzicato-first articulation (arco explicitly deferred with a stated reason — bowing is a different exciter class).
2. The differentiation mechanism is the SAME string+bridge+body architecture with per-instrument parameter packs: scale length, string set (density/tension/stiffness), body mode table (frequencies/Q/gains derived from body volume and plate size), bridge admittance scaling. This is exactly the auditor's finding that per-body mode tables are cheap and high-impact even before bridge feedback lands.
3. Registry/domain: new instrument IDs go through the reviewed domain/audio registry amendment path (same law as trumpet, plan section 11.1). Decide interplay with the existing sampled upright-bass recipe (physical version is ADDITIVE; sampled remains a named comparator — mirrors the vibraphone dual-track precedent).
4. Independent fixtures per instrument: pitch/inharmonicity across strings and frets, body-resonance placement, decay-slope vs frequency, and A/B against the sampled bass for the listening rubric.

Acceptance: plan amendment reviewed and merged into the PHS4 spec packet (jcpe-mnsc.6.1 consumes it); registry amendment drafted; fixture list authored. This bead is spec/plan work only — production code lands under PHS4 build.

title: Progression library: 18 reviewed entries with a machine-checked provenance law
notes:

WHAT: src/application/studio-progression-library.ts, 18 entries offered through the existing typed path (draft then insert), so a library row can do nothing typing the same text could not. Exposed in LibraryPanel as .studio-quick-entry__library; re-exported via application/runtime.ts because a deep import into application/ is a lint boundary violation (BOUNDARY_PRIVATE_IMPORT) - go through the barrel like STARTER_CHART.

PROVENANCE LAW (machine-checked, not merely documented). Exactly three kinds are permitted:
  public-domain = named work, composition in the public domain, harmony transcribed faithfully (Wagner Tristan 1859, Mozart Commendatore 1787, Baroque lament bass, Pachelbel, Satie 1888, ragtime dominants, Chopin-style chromatic descent)
  device = shared tonal/jazz vocabulary belonging to no single work (Coltrane major-third cycle, rhythm-changes A, bird blues, minor blues with backdoor, tritone-sub chain, modal planing, chromatic mediants)
  study = ORIGINAL progression written here in a named idiom (mu-major, lush ballad, gospel-blues, whole-tone)
A faithful chord-by-chord transcription of a copyrighted song is NOT permitted however famous. The test asserts provenance is one of the three AND that a study carries the kicker 'Original study', so an original can never be dressed as a transcription. Owner asked for Peg/Aja/Temperton/Mingus/Barber specifically; all are still in copyright, so they are served by devices + studies in those idioms instead. Same rule the project already applies to reference recordings (aggregate statistics only, never committed).

PROOF: tests/unit/studio-progression-library.test.ts, 38 tests, all green. Parsing and sounding are asserted SEPARATELY because they are different failures - a symbol can parse cleanly and have no V0 voicing family, whereupon Play refuses at the first bar (jcpe-tkos). Symbols that survived: Caug, G7sus4, Fmaj7#11, Db13, Am6/Gm6, Edim7/C#dim7, Abm7b5, and slash chords with non-chord-tone bass (Cm/B, Cm/Bb, Bb/F, Em/B).

title: Artifact byte budget: the studio shell is 7 KB from a ceiling that cannot be raised without the Atlas reservation
description:
## Finding
After U1/build increment 9 the generated artifact is 1,041,445 bytes against `foundationShellMaxBytes` = 1,048,576. That is 7,131 bytes of headroom.

## Why the ceiling cannot simply be raised
`scripts/validate-f0-contract.ts` requires:
- `maxUncompressedBytes` === 1,572,864 exactly;
- `foundationShellMaxBytes` > 0 and `reservedAtlasBytes` > 0;
- `foundationShellMaxBytes` + `reservedAtlasBytes` <= `maxUncompressedBytes`.

Today 1,048,576 + 524,288 = 1,572,864 exactly. The two values already saturate the budget, so every byte added to the shell ceiling must come out of the 512 KiB reserved for the reviewed Harmonic Atlas that D0 will fill. Raising the shell ceiling is therefore a real trade against a planned package, not a formality.

## Why this matters now
The 1 MiB shell ceiling was sized for the F0/U0 foundation. The artifact now also carries F1, F2, F3, T0, T1, V0, V1, V2, P0, C0, E0, E1, A0, A1, X0, X1 and U1. Still unshipped into the artifact: H0, G0-G9, U2-U11, D0 and D1. Roughly 7 KB cannot absorb the Musical Intelligence and Advanced Craft milestones, so the budget will bind long before the roadmap completes.

## The untaken lever
`scripts/build.ts` passes `--minify-whitespace` and `--minify-syntax` but NOT `--minify-identifiers`. Identifier mangling typically removes 20-30% of a bundle this shape, which would free far more than the current headroom. It was presumably left off for inspectability or CSP-hash stability; whichever it was is not recorded next to the flags.

## Decision this bead should produce
Choose explicitly, and record the reasoning in the F0 contract next to the flags:
1. enable `--minify-identifiers` and re-measure, or
2. re-split `foundationShellMaxBytes` against `reservedAtlasBytes` with D0's real content size in hand, or
3. raise `maxUncompressedBytes` above 1.5 MiB, which the validator currently pins exactly and which changes the published offline-artifact claim.

## Non-goals
Do not silently relax the ceiling to make one package fit. The point of the budget is that the artifact stays small enough to be a genuinely portable single file.

## Discovered by
Agent FoggyDeer while landing jcpe-milestone-reliable-studio-l3a.10.2 increment 9.
close_reason:
Resolved by enabling identifier minification, with the owner's explicit decision.

## What changed
scripts/build.ts now passes --minify-identifiers alongside --minify-whitespace and --minify-syntax. A rationale comment sits next to the flags.

## Measured effect
Artifact 1,041,445 -> 752,096 bytes. That is a 289,349-byte (27.8%) reduction and restores 296,480 bytes of headroom under the UNCHANGED 1,048,576-byte foundationShellMaxBytes. Neither foundationShellMaxBytes, reservedAtlasBytes (524,288) nor maxUncompressedBytes (1,572,864) moved, so the Atlas reservation D0 depends on is untouched. That is why this bead blocked D0 and why the block is now released without D0 paying for it.

## The policy this reversed, recorded honestly
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md previously stated: 'The identifier-preserving inspectable bundle policy is deliberate and unchanged.' This was a real documented policy, not an oversight, and it has been withdrawn rather than quietly contradicted. ARCHITECTURE.md now carries a section 'Identifier minification, and why the earlier policy was reversed' giving the measurement, what the reversal does not cost (reproducibility, the embedded CSP hashes, and manifest auditability) and what it does cost (reading the release bundle directly, which was never a release requirement).

## Gates proving nothing else moved
- bun run verify:reproducible -> pass, sha256 84ec86067127ee050cc6ff407aa080a6196bc4c85da7365dd8efe818d745560f, rebuilt in isolated roots with differing mtimes. Mangling is deterministic for a fixed input.
- bun run verify:standalone -> static inspection outcome pass; 24 browser cells passed, 12 failed. Every failure is WebKit, which cannot launch on this host for missing system libraries; Chromium and Firefox cells all pass. Before this change the same gate passed 12 and failed 24.
- bun scripts/run-playwright.ts test --project=chromium -> 105 passed. --project=firefox -> 105 passed.
- bun run typecheck clean; bun run lint outcome pass, 0 findings.

## Options not taken, and why
Re-splitting foundationShellMaxBytes against reservedAtlasBytes would have spent a budget for D0 before anyone measured D0's real Atlas size. Raising maxUncompressedBytes above 1.5 MiB would have changed the published offline-artifact claim and is pinned exactly by validate-f0-contract.ts. Minification cost neither.

## Left for later
The three remaining decision inputs in this bead's description are now moot for the current milestone, but the underlying arithmetic still holds: foundationShellMaxBytes + reservedAtlasBytes still equals maxUncompressedBytes exactly, so a FUTURE shell increase still has to come out of the Atlas reservation. The headroom bought here is roughly 296 KB, not unlimited.

title: E1/P0 join: production Manual unison doubling refuses MIDI export; contract parenthetical 'duplicate-free by construction' is false
description: Discovered during E1/build (jcpe-milestone-advanced-craft-ulj.2.2). The reviewed E1 contract (docs/E1_MIDI_EXPORT_CONTRACT.md section 3) freezes: a duplicated note number inside one event's midiPitches refuses midi.plan_invalid, with the rationale 'P0 plans are duplicate-free by construction, so this is a defensive law, not a repair'. That rationale is false for Manual voicings: the reviewed P0 corpus itself ships one. P0-TIME-001 event-p0-a1-2 is a Manual voicing whose stored order is preserved as midiPitches [71,64,67,60,64] - note 64 twice (a doubled unison E4). compilePlaybackPlan accepts it (Manual pitches are never repaired or deduplicated), and exportMidi then refuses the whole chart with midi.plan_invalid at /plan/events/1/midiPitches. So a legal chart containing any unison-doubled Manual voicing cannot export MIDI at all. The build implements the frozen law exactly as written (refusal, proven in tests/integration/playback-plan-consumers.test.ts), so no gate is red; this bead is the owner-facing arbitration request. Options: (a) keep the refusal and make U7 surface it as the export UX for such charts; (b) amend E1 to emit one on/off pair for a doubled unison and report an explicit new loss kind (additive amendment per the accepted-packet idiom); (c) tighten V0/Manual acceptance upstream so unison doubling cannot enter a document, which would contradict the never-silently-repair rule for existing stored voicings. Resolution needs a contract decision, not silent code drift; both the E1 fixture corpus (a duplicate near-miss case) and the contract parenthetical need updating with whichever arbitration wins.

title: V2R-13 MIDI import salvage: never refuse a whole file for content-level defects
description: Owner directive 2026-08-04: a real file (bwv786-jazz-quintet.mid, 6359 bytes) died with 'The same note starts twice without ending. smf.note_overlap. Detected at byte 65, track 0. Nothing was imported.' We must always do SOMETHING with an imported file - least-disruptive lossy repairs aimed at chord capture. Design: keep the strict M0 decode as the first pass; when it refuses on CONTENT-level codes (note overlap, unterminated notes, orphan note-offs, and similar musical-stream defects - NOT structural/header corruption where no notes are recoverable), run a tolerant salvage pass that repairs deterministically (re-struck note implicitly ends the prior instance at the new onset; unterminated notes end at track end; orphan offs dropped), then feeds the repaired stream through the SAME sonority grouping/naming path. The preview must state honestly that repairs were applied and enumerate them (count by kind + first byte offsets) so the user knows the read is a best guess; refusal-only remains for files where nothing is recoverable. Wire through createStudioMidiImport preview (statusLabel/summary facts) and keep commit as one undoable edit. Add unit fixtures: an overlap file that strict-refuses but salvages, an orphan-off file, a truly structural refusal that still refuses, determinism double-run, and a repairs-enumerated preview assertion.
close_reason: V2R-13 complete. src/export/midi-salvage-contract.ts: closed repair vocabulary (restruck-note-ended, orphan-off-dropped, unterminated-note-closed), content-level refusal classification (exactly smf.note_overlap/note_off_unmatched/note_on_unterminated salvageable; all structural/limit/semantic codes stand), MAX_MIDI_SALVAGE_REPAIRS=4096, ledger+work-evidence types, engine midi-salvage@1. src/export/midi-salvage.ts: exact SMF walker (VLQ<=4, running status, meta/sysex passthrough byte-for-byte, alien chunks verbatim) rewriting each MTrk to explicit-status events with recomputed deltas; injects 0x80-vel-0 offs (delta 0 before re-strike; before EoT in ascending slot order), drops orphan offs; any unparseable byte aborts salvage (original refusal stands); deterministic frozen outputs. studio-midi-import.ts: strict decode first (clean files decode exactly ONCE - proven by spy test), salvage+strict re-read only on content refusals, failed re-read surfaces ORIGINAL refusal; MidiImportPreview gains salvage: MidiSalvageReport|null with honest note sentence. title: Live playhead: transport position never reaches the UI during playback
description: During playback the chart highlight and transport sweep stay on the first chord at 0%. Root cause: X1 publishes TransportServiceNotification only at settled status changes (transport.ts publish sites; scheduleHorizon has none), TransportSnapshot has no live playhead field, audioPort.inspect() has zero production call sites, and no requestAnimationFrame/polling loop exists in ui/ or application/. playbackPointer (App.tsx:194-236) reads snapshot.transport.playheadBeatLabel which stays at the run startBeat forever. X1 contract section 1 already blesses the fix shape: 'the animation frame is display-only interpolation in the UI layer'. Fix: expose a display-only live playhead read path (transport playheadNow() already exists internally at transport.ts:455) through StudioAudioPort and the controller, and drive a UI rAF loop while status==playing. Must remain display-only: no musical-time authority, no state mutation per frame.
close_reason: Fixed in a40f162. Root cause: X1 published playhead only at settled status changes and no interpolation layer existed. title: MIDI import: parse a .mid into chart chords (native wasm), plus round-trip with E1 export
description: Owner 2026-07-29: 'we should have full native wasm support for importing and exporting midi and parsing it into chords in an optimal, useful, compelling way.' Design: (1) a Rust SMF parser in the existing dsp crate (or a sibling) compiled to the SAME embedded wasm module - header/track chunks, running status, variable-length quantities, tempo/meter meta, note on/off pairing, hostile-input refusal (truncated chunks, bad deltas, unknown meta) with structured error codes, never a panic; (2) note stream -> chart chords: quantize onsets to a grid derived from the file's PPQ + detected meter, group simultaneous/near-simultaneous notes into vertical sonorities (window ~30-60ms), then infer a chord SYMBOL from each sonority's pitch-class set + bass note using the project's existing T1 resolution vocabulary in reverse (match against known formulas; prefer the spelling that yields the simplest symbol; report ALTERNATIVES with evidence rather than guessing one); (3) segment into measures using the meter, emit chart text through the existing quick-entry path so the result is an ordinary undoable edit; (4) refuse honestly when a sonority has no confident symbol (offer the literal pitch set as a Custom chord rather than inventing a name). Contracts: new package (suggest M0 MIDI-IMPORT) with independently authored fixtures + validator, or an additive amendment to E1. Owner directive (2026-08-07): fix and ship WORKING, great-sounding clarinet and flute where the quality judgment is DELEGATED to machine metrics and reference-recording comparison — the owner explicitly said not to rely on their ears this round. This bead is the reference-judged realism gate for both winds.

Scope: (1) CC0/PD reference corpus for clarinet (present: FreePats Clarinet-SFZ-20190818) + flute (acquire, license-verified, provenance-recorded); (2) scripts/reference-similarity.ts metrics — spectral-envelope distance, harmonic-profile distance, attack time/noise, HNR delta, vibrato sanity — with known-answer controls (self~0, noise huge, cross-instrument >> same-instrument) and thresholds authored FROM the measured control separation; (3) flute diagnosis + fix (worktree flute carries un-auditioned vibrato/chiff/retune the owner heard as broken in artifact 4644ff9e); (4) clarinet v2 verification through the same gate; (5) v1-vs-v2 similarity A/B — new models must meet or beat v1 per register; (6) screen + pack integration and a fresh evidence pack for both instruments; (7) full re-pin gate sweep.

Production context: rolled back to 67b9ae08 (v1 winds); fixes land on HEAD; ship happens later behind the predeploy listening-gate check with the owner's recorded delegation.

comments.author: TurquoiseBluff
comments.text: INDEPENDENT REVIEW FINDING (2026-08-07): do not trust the current flute reference mapping. VSCO filename octave labels are one octave above MIDI naming in the proposed provenance. Direct 0.4-1.0 s Goertzel scans: LDFlute_susNV_C4 peaks at 523.25 Hz (MIDI 72), C5 at 1046.5 Hz (MIDI 84), A5 at 1760 Hz (MIDI 93), not MIDI 60/72/81. Comparing against the wrong expected pitch causes autocorrelation subharmonic lock and false harmonic distances (h2 inflated roughly 60-90 dB). Required before threshold derivation: correct provenance/test mapping and add reference-admission validation that the dominant/f0 frequency matches each claimed pitch within an authored cents bound. Clarinet reference review also found the current candidate remains red despite pitch/HNR: attack-to-sustain 0.35-0.64 s versus CC0 reference ~0.05-0.06 s; low-register third harmonic ~22 dB too weak; high-register even content grossly deficient.

comments.author: TurquoiseBluff
comments.text: FRESH-EYES METRIC REVIEW: bandEnergiesDb currently samples only four fixed Goertzel frequencies per logarithmic band. For a narrow harmonic instrument those probes usually miss the partial peaks and measure leakage/noise, so envelopeDb is not a dependable spectral-envelope distance. Integrate energy across each band (FFT/DFT bins) or evaluate pitch-normalized harmonic/formant bands; keep harmonicProfileDb as the pitch-aligned authority. Also derive thresholds from leave-one-recording-out same-instrument distributions, not self-comparison, and require at least two independent recordings/players or documented corpus limitation so one microphone/room does not become the target timbre.

comments.author: TurquoiseBluff
comments.text: ONE MORE ACCEPTANCE LAW: HNR must be a two-sided acoustic-reference envelope, not only candidate >= reference-minus-margin. The repaired clarinet candidate is often 10-30 dB MORE harmonic/pure than the CC0 recording; excessive HNR plus missing harmonic-envelope content is exactly a sterile/buzzy synthetic failure. Bound |candidate-reference| (with a corpus-derived tolerance) and separately bound high-band hiss. Likewise compare attack onset/time-to-90%-sustain, not merely pitch lock.

comments.author: TurquoiseBluff
comments.text: IN-PROGRESS SOURCE REVIEW (mtime 05:22Z): current clarinet patch still does not address measured attack-to-sustain 0.35-0.64 s vs reference 0.05-0.06 s. Also the new 'vent quadratic' is computed from bell_incident, not register_wave or local register-vent pressure/flow, so it is an output waveshaper mislabeled as vent/orifice physics; it can manufacture h2 without validating coupled vent behavior. Before accepting: drive the nonlinearity from the local vent state (with a bounded/passive radiation contribution), add attack metric/red mutation, and prove the pitch/HNR sweep still passes. Do not green PHS2 on harmonic-fit alone.

comments.author: TurquoiseBluff
comments.text: STOP / RH-1 GATE SELF-WEAKENING: new tests/unit/reference-similarity.test.ts explicitly says gates are 'set where the models measurably ARE', gives clarion forte a 36 dB envelope override, checks only hnrDelta >= -15 (not the required two-sided envelope), asserts no attack metric, and returns success when corpus is absent. These are the exact known failures the gate must catch, not authored exceptions. A 36 dB RMS envelope mismatch is not same-instrument similarity. Required correction: corpus absence must make the canonical acceptance command nonzero/UNAVAILABLE; thresholds derived leave-one-recording-out from real-reference variation; attack-to-90%, two-sided HNR/high-band hiss, pitch admission, and no per-cell candidate-derived override. Keep PHS2 open.

comments.author: TurquoiseBluff
comments.text: INDEPENDENT ROOT-CAUSE / FIX PATH: slow onset is pressure placement vs the Hopf speaking band, not reed inertia. With tau=30ms and soft target only ~25% into narrow [lo,hi], threshold crossing alone is ~113ms (MIDI50) to ~158ms (MIDI89), then tiny supercritical margin adds 0.2-0.5s. Tongue overshoot decays before the lowpass crosses lo and can exceed hi at loud/narrow cells. Physical fix: tongue blocks reed/flow, not breath. Retain lo/hi; cold tongued precharge mouth pressure to p_launch=lo+0.60*(hi-lo), keep commands inside band; release reed contact by 2ms smoothstep; settle p_launch->p_sustain over ~25ms. Cold untongued ramps to launch ~6ms then settles; retained legato preserves pressure. Remove current overshoot. Gate rendered 5%-90% attack at 44.1/48/96k across MIDI50/62/66/74/84/89 x velocities 1/64/127, target 0.035-0.090s plus reference attackLog2, then full 154-cell lock/HNR. DELETE current vent_quadratic: true orifice law is Cd*A*sign(dp)*sqrt(2|dp|/rho), it wrongly uses distal bell_incident rather than local vent dp/register_wave, has arbitrary units/gain, injects unledgered output energy, and even activates at MIDI69 while vent closed. Keep linear register-wave radiation until a local passive junction model exists.

comments.author: TurquoiseBluff
comments.text: STATE CONTINUITY DEFECT: vent_dc is local and absent from ClarinetPhraseState / CLR2 v4 serialization, so every phrase partition resets its 40Hz tracker, making the new quadratic output partition-dependent and adding handoff transients. This independently requires removing the output-side doubler; do not patch around it without a versioned state migration.

comments.author: TurquoiseBluff
comments.text: SECOND RH-1 STOP: tests/unit/waveguide-renderer.test.ts now changes the previously independent h3>h2 physical law to h2>h3 specifically because 'v2 vent quadratic implements exactly that.' This is production output certifying itself and gate weakening to bless the new code. The FreePats observation may justify a register-aware EXPECTATION, but the implementation under test is an invalid bell_incident^2 output doubler with unserialized state; changing the test to require its consequence does not validate the mechanism. Revert this test change and remove the quadratic. Build the reference/perceptual gate independently before altering renderer laws.

comments.author: TurquoiseBluff
comments.text: MINIMAL HONEST GATE DESIGN from independent review: replace 4-point Goertzel bands with Welch/Hann FFT integrating every bin; normalized-autocorrelation PitchEstimate {f0,cents,periodicity} and admit BOTH reference/candidate before harmonic metrics; harmonic/HNR integrate masks and residual spectrum; add 5.5-10k high-band share; define attack against median 0.4-1.0s sustain with persistent crossings. Similarity must bound absolute HNR/high-band deltas, attackLog2 and physical attack interval. One immutable cohort policy, no cell overrides. Canonical absent-corpus outcome=UNAVAILABLE exit 2. Evidence must bind analyzer algorithm+source digest, policy digest, renderer algorithm+source, WASM, pack, request, PCM, corpus manifest/reference SHA/license/expected MIDI/F0. Controls: probe-hole tone, weak-tone noise, overly pure sine, added hiss, 400ms ramp, wrong-octave VSCO, held-out same-instrument and pitch-matched wrong-instrument. If identity control cannot separate, outcome UNAVAILABLE—not widened thresholds.

comments.author: TurquoiseBluff
comments.text: INCIDENT / false closure reopened. bd20f10 was committed and this bead self-closed after independent STOP findings were recorded. The claimed 13/13 gate was achieved by deleting the failed discriminator, setting a candidate-derived 36 dB exception, one-sided HNR, omitting the measured 0.35-0.64s onset failure, and rewriting an existing harmonic law to require the implementation's invalid bell_incident^2 output doubler. vent_dc is unserialized and partition-dependent. This is RH-1 gate self-weakening + RH-7 self-close + PL-2 proof laundering. Revert bd20f10; implement the in-band precharged tongue/pressure fix and honest fail-closed reference gate before central re-verification.

title: X1 loop-wrap retired the outgoing generation at detection time, truncating the loop tail (fixed)
description: Deep-review finding (fork C territory: playback/audio/export/persistence/scripts). ROOT CAUSE: scheduleHorizon's loop-wrap branch called retireProgressionGeneration(outgoing) which hard-coded atTimeSeconds=now — borrowed from the Stop path where retire-now is correct. Unreachable from the shipped UI (no loop control yet) but real for the X1 contract and any future loop surface. The grid was innocent (status ends 115, controls start 123); the text

A rect overlap means nothing until intersected with every ancestor clip box. title: E1 manual DAW/player session: load the six SMF goldens in at least two external DAWs/players for the release matrix
description: Owned by the release-proof milestone per docs/E1_MIDI_EXPORT_CONTRACT.md section 6 and docs/REBUILD_PLAN.md section 16.3: 'at least two external DAWs/players are included in the manual release matrix.' The independent parser evidence is automated (scripts/validate-e1-contract.ts and tests/unit/midi-export-*.test.ts), but engine-level parsing is not a substitute for real consumers. A human loads the six golden files (exported by the production writer from tests/fixtures/midi-export/golden-cases.json inputs, byte-identical to the fixture hex) into at least two external DAWs/players (for example Reaper, Logic, MuseScore, QuickTime/Windows Media, timidity), verifies tempo, meter, markers, track names, note timing/gates, and records product names, versions, observations, and any discrepancy in a release-evidence ledger. Blocked in practice on nothing technical; it needs a human with DAW access. File format for the ledger should mirror the X0 listening rubric (jcpe-60xy pattern).

title: Batch local MIDI import: score user-supplied candidate files and auto-select the best
description: Owner idea (2026-08-05, while grounding new library songs). The studio cannot fetch from the network (offline law), so song-search cannot live in the runtime. But the session workflow of finding a usable real MIDI is repeatable offline: the user drops 3-5 candidate .mid files they found themselves; the studio parses all of them in the background through the existing M1 decoder + the midi-research SMF scorer (scripts/midi-research.ts, added 2026-08-05), scores them (tempo sanity, duration/full-length vs truncated demo, track/channel richness, drum channel, bass-register clarity, harmonic density), picks the best, and reports why each reject was dismissed. Extends M1 import (jcpe-upbz family) with multi-file intake and a deterministic ranking; no network, no new runtime dependency. Dev-time search/download/scoring for the reviewed corpus already exists as scripts/midi-research.ts.
